places.place: Acceptance.lean: acceptance_factorization, every_optimum_has_access_iff, maintenance_weight_exact, unavoidable_score_loss, approximate_score_bound, stale_value_shield_suboptimal
places.states: The module's general law concerns choices best among an allowed set under an integer score. With a positive lift, a choice is best under the score with acceptance exactly when it accepts and its move is best under the base score, so every best choice keeps access exactly when every best base move does. Its other results are general bounds (the loss from restricting moves; best by an estimate within err gives within 2*err of every allowed move) and Bool-built cases: diverting beats maintaining, a fixed weight for keeping access works exactly when it exceeds the diversion value, and a stale value prefers a branch the restriction forbids.
places.moves: S: `Best` (l.49) is a choice among `allowed : A → Prop` by a score. `acceptance_factorization` (l.65): for any allowed set, base score q and lift > 0, a pair (move, accept bit) is Best under `AcceptScore` iff the bit is true and the move is Best under q. `every_optimum_has_access_iff` (l.89): every best choice keeps `access` iff every best base move does. `no_base_optimal_access` (l.97): where no best base move keeps access, no best move does. There is no `Process S A`; it is a one-shot choice.
places.reading: S (only an estimate, no observation class): `approximate_score_bound` (l.275): where an `estimate` is within `err` of `actual` on allowed moves, a choice Best by the estimate is within 2*err of every allowed move; `approximate_score_bound_tight` (l.291) shows the bound attained. B: `stale_value_shield_suboptimal` (l.241): a value computed without the restriction (`UnrestrictedValue`) makes branch true best, though its allowed continuations score 1 and branch false scores 2; `recomputed_value_restores_branch` (l.258). No class of things read alike was found.
places.level: N: the resource that keeps a change possible occurs only as a Bool divert bit (`MaintenanceValue`, l.106; `Maintains`, l.111). No amount runs down.
places.giving: N
places.cost: S: `unavoidable_score_loss` (l.183): the loss q u - q v of a restricted best move v against an unrestricted best u is nonnegative and least among the allowed moves. `maintenance_weight_exact` (l.163): maintaining forgoes the diversion value, and every best choice maintains iff diversion < weight. `fixed_access_weight_boundary` (l.144) and `every_fixed_access_weight_has_counterexample` (l.151): every fixed weight is defeated by some larger diversion value.
places.no_return: N: `accepting_optimum_can_destroy_access` (l.136) shows a best choice that diverts (¬ Maintains true). It is a one-shot choice with no later steps and nothing about regaining.
places.both_outcomes: S (keeping or losing access, Bool model with general integers): `maintenance_weight_exact` (l.163): every best choice keeps access iff diversion < weight, the tie counted among the failures. `maintenance_separation` (l.114): with diversion > 0 and lift > 0, a choice is best iff it is (divert, accept).
places.comparison: S: `every_optimum_has_access_iff` (l.89) carries the access property between best choices under the score with acceptance and best base moves. `acceptance_factorization` (l.65) is the carrying law. `unrestricted_value_optimal` (l.228) and `restricted_value_bounds` (l.216) compare two value functions on the two-step model (B).

Under the whole-run reading every comparison satisfying C prefers the course without it (for malignant, built). General laws: the whole-run reading withholds every event of a consuming formation, and living significance on it holds iff active events of non-consuming formations fall under relevance. places.states: One built process, `installation` on `State` with moves probe/issue/deliver/enact. Each move draws one unit of reserve and one unit of time before a deadline, and fails where its conditions do not hold. Laws over all states of this model: protocol and plan runs are traces (protocol_iff, run_iff, passes_iff), reserve + drawn is invariant, and the protocol completes under signed, current, open route, reserve ≥ 3 and three time units. The rest are computed cases.
places.moves: B (laws over all states of one model): `installation` (l.267) is a `Process State Move`. `chosen_completes` (l.318): a plan chosen for a list of states has a completed trace from each. `none_chosen` (l.325): where none is chosen for two states, no plan of the repertoire completes from both. `unsigned_no_issue`, `stale_no_issue`, `undelivered_no_enact`, `revoked_no_enact` (l.341–358) disable moves. `statewise_not_uniform` (l.512): each of two states has its own protocol trace, but no single plan completes from both.
places.reading: B: `probe` (l.123) answers whether the route is open, and a plan branches on the answer. `omitted_route_fails` (l.528): a plan selected from a list omitting the open-route state completes from the state it models and has no trace from the one it omits. `unknown_route_probes` (l.450) and `known_route_no_probe` (l.455): what is listed decides which plan is selected.
places.level: B: `reserve` and `time`/`deadline` in State. `draw` (l.87) fails unless amount ≤ reserve and time + delay ≤ deadline. `protocol_exact` (l.204) needs reserve ≥ 3 and three time units. `late_probe_no_run` (l.469): the slow inquiry misses the deadline. `shutdown_trace` (l.551) ends with reserve 0. Nothing replenishes, so nothing comes back.
places.giving: N: the reserve is a field. Nothing gives to it.
places.cost: B: every move that draws spends the installation's own reserve and time: `move_draws` (l.408), `draw_conserves` (l.165). The inquiry costs too (`probe`). `timely_trace` (l.538) vs `late_no_trace` (l.545): an equally accurate but slower inquiry spends the time the protocol needed.
places.multiplying: N: `generation` and `version` are counters (replacement_trace l.561, update_trace l.571). No units leave units.
places.no_return: N: no stated irreversibility. reserve + drawn is conserved (`conserved_invariant`), but no statement says the reserve or running, once lost, is not regained.
places.both_outcomes: B in part: `passes_iff` (l.309): a plan passes exactly when the installation has a trace along it ending completed. This is completion, not going on or ending. `timely_trace`/`late_no_trace` and `shutdown_trace` are built pairs.
places.comparison: S (within the model): `protocol_iff` (l.284) and `run_iff` (l.299) carry between the partial-function protocol/run and traces of the process `installation`. `statewise_not_uniform` (l.512) compares per-state paths with a uniform plan.
places.rank: B: a deadline. `draw` requires time + delay ≤ deadline, `draw_conserves` (l.165) keeps time ≤ deadline, and `late_probe_no_run` (l.469) / `late_no_trace` (l.545) show runs failing on it.
places.closed_region: S (within the model): `conserved_invariant` (l.426): reserve + drawn = c is an `Invariant installation`. `conserved_trace` (l.433): every trace keeps it.
places.forms_change: B (weak): `replacement_trace` (l.561) completes with generation advanced by one, and `update_trace` (l.571) with version advanced by one, while running stays true. These are counters, not kinds coming and going.

places.states: General laws for every web and flow. Gaining support needs a rise, and in a balanced flow where only active formations give and activity needs support, every rise is given by a supported formation. So once no member of a closed family (or nothing at all) is supported, none is again, and support recurring with bounded spells is passed on by newer gainers. For a part withheld: the levels without it are unique, the difference is exact, support holds exactly within the part's net-draw margin, and parts that give at least, at most or exactly what they take close, open or change nothing by inclusion of what is admitted. Built witnesses (Restoring.*) show each premise of the absorbing end is needed, Inflow widens, and Transfer is mixed.

places.reading: S in part (no observation class): `Web.Admits` (l.378), and `supported_iff_admits` (l.435): support is admission by the standing levels. `not_arises_of_unchanged` (l.424): a formation active exactly where supported, whose requirements, needs and levels stay across a step, does not arise across it.
places.level: S: levels of conditions with needs. `Flow.Balances` (level(t+1) + taken = level t + given) is a premise throughout. `Balances.supported_iff_within_margin` (l.633): f is supported at t iff, on each condition it requires, need + the part's taken so far ≤ level without the part + the part's given so far. `fitsBand_iff_within_margins_at` (l.670) adds a cap. What comes back is given only by supported formations (`rise_given_by_supported`, l.178), so return depends on what is supported, that is on levels.
places.giving: S: `rise_given_by_supported` (l.178): under Balances, Acting (only active formations give) and Dependent (active only where supported), every rise is given by a present formation that is supported. `gains_from_supported` (l.214). `unsupported_stays` (l.330): if no member is supported at T, requirements do not loosen and only members give to what members require, no member is supported later. So what gives is a formation of the model that can lose support. B: Restoring.Inflow, Idle, Carried, Spontaneous, Adapting (l.724–873) each break one premise and support returns.
places.cost: N: no statement says giving costs the giver. Transfer's conveyor (l.891) takes from one condition and gives to another, as a built flow.
places.no_return: S (concluded, at the loss of the givers): `Flow.unsupported_stays` (l.330) and `unsupported_stays_at` (l.308): once no member is supported, none is supported at any later step, under Balances, Acting, Dependent, unloosened and closure ('within'). `nothing_supported_stays` (l.360): once nothing is supported, nothing is supported or active again. B: the Restoring witnesses show each premise is needed.
places.both_outcomes: S (support kept or lost, general): `Balances.supported_iff_within_margin` (l.633) and `supported_iff_within_margin_at` (l.596): supported at t exactly when the part's net draw stays within the margin. `fitsBand_iff_within_margins_at` (l.670). places.comparison: S: `Web.Includes` (l.388) and `Exceeds` (l.392), a preorder (`Includes.refl` l.444, `Includes.trans` l.448), and `Includes.not_exceeded` (l.453). `Balances.withheld` (l.562): an exact difference between levels with and without the part. `WithheldLevels.unique` (l.532). `Balances.closes_nothing` (l.642): a part giving each condition at least what it takes gives levels including those without it. `opens_nothing` (l.650), `changes_nothing` (l.658). `Admits.mono` (l.439): admission is closed upward in levels. B: `Restoring.Inflow.widens` (l.786), `Transfer.mixed` (l.983).
places.rank: N: no rank or bound in this module's statements. D: the account points to `Flow.excess_bounded` and `Flow.joint_excess_ends` in Becoming.Continuation.
places.closed_region: S: `unsupported_stays` (l.330): the set 'no member supported' is closed under steps, given the premises (an absorbing region). `nothing_supported_stays` (l.360) for the whole.
places.forms_change: S: `Flow.support_passes_on` (l.282): under Balances, Acting, Dependent, requirements never loosening, `brief` (no formation supported K+1 steps in a row) and `recurs` (some gain at arbitrarily late steps), for every T and N it is not refutable that some gain from N on is given by a supported formation that itself gained support after T. Support goes on as a relay of newer gainers. Also `gain_given_by_recent_gainer` (l.265). B: `Restoring.Inflow.widens` (l.786): with the giver's part, the levels include and exceed those without it, a widening.

places.place: Change.lean: over_stretch, family_over_stretch, fallen_within, rising_recurs, falling_recurs, held_over_stretch, keep_pace, coming_recurs_iff, Web.unceasing_iff, persists, stays_failing, buqiong_alike_iff, positions_iff_em, Accretion, Attrition
places.states: S: General laws of every unfolding with no premise about it. Over any stretch, an amount at the end plus what it fell equals the amount at the start plus what it rose, for one amount and for a finite family (over_stretch l.173, family_over_stretch l.187). From this: falls are bounded by the start total plus rises (fallen_within l.217); falling at arbitrarily late steps needs rising at arbitrarily late steps (rising_recurs l.254); and in a finite family coming to be recurs exactly when ceasing to be recurs (coming_recurs_iff l.457, Web.arising_recurs_iff l.542, Web.unceasing_iff l.568, Web.standing_recurs_iff l.529). The grammar readings (ceasesToBe_iff_wang l.686, sheng_iff_change l.732, buqiong_alike_iff l.783, persists_of_positions l.807, positions_iff_em l.865, core_iff_same_course l.884) are general. Only Accretion (l.578) and Attrition (l.603) are built webs.
places.moves: N: No Process S A, policy, plan or allowed set. Every law is about one fixed unfolding (amounts q : Nat → Nat, determinations p : Nat → Prop, or one Web).
places.reading: S: The class Steps.alike p reads steps alike by a determination. sheng_iff_change (l.732): with p decided, step t+1 begins under that class exactly when p comes to be or ceases across t. continues_in_core_iff_buqiong (l.899): a step continues under the core of the class exactly when the line under the class never ends from it. positions_iff_em (l.865): deciding every position of every determination is exactly excluded middle. No observation, and no rule made from what is registered, decides an outcome.
places.share: N: No share or fraction, and no rule set again from one.
places.level: S: Amounts q : Nat → Nat with rise and fall (l.159, l.163). fallen_within (l.217): over any stretch a finite family falls by at most its start total more than it rises. rising_recurs (l.254) and Web.falls_need_rises (l.522): levels of finitely many conditions that fall at arbitrarily late steps rise at arbitrarily late steps. risen_within and falling_recurs (l.224, l.263) need a bound B. Nothing states what comes back as depending on what is left.
places.giving: N: Rises are only differences of the given amount function; no going-on of the model gives them. Web.supported_of (l.513) takes as a premise that dependences, needs and levels are kept between two steps.
places.multiplying: N: No units leaving units. B: Accretion.web (l.582) has formation f arise at step f, so new formations arise ever (Accretion.unceasing l.589), but not by a law of offspring.
places.no_return: S: stays_failing (l.341): what fails at S and comes to be at no later step fails at every later step. The no-return is the premise (no coming to be), not concluded. persists (l.323) and persists_of_em (l.349) are the same for holding. B: Attrition.nothing_arises (l.617): each formation ceases at step f and nothing arises, built.
places.both_outcomes: S: coming_recurs_iff (l.457): in a finite family of decided determinations, coming to be recurs exactly when ceasing to be recurs. Web.unceasing_iff (l.568): with finitely many formations and activity decided, some formation arises at arbitrarily late steps exactly when some ceases at arbitrarily late steps. Web.unceasing_iff_covering (l.550) asks only for a list covering the active formations from some step on. All general. These are exactly-whens between arising and ceasing recurring, not between going on and ending. B: Accretion and Attrition show that each direction fails without finiteness.
places.comparison: S: core_iff_same_course (l.884): two steps lie in one class of the core of Steps.alike p exactly when p agrees at every pair of steps equally far after them. Steps.course_of_constant (l.874): a constant relation carries its pairs along every later step. Web.supported_of (l.513): support at s is carried to t where each dependence at t was had at s, at no greater need, on a level no lower.
places.rank: N: No variant or rank that falls, and no deadline. fallen_within (l.217) bounds the total fall, not when anything ends.
places.closed_region: S: persists (l.323): a decided determination holding at S that ceases at no later step holds at every later step. still_of_buqiong (l.789): where the line under the class never ends from S, nothing comes to be or ceases from S on. still_stays_of_constant (l.909): under a class constant along the steps, a determination unchanged across one step is unchanged across the next.
places.forms_change: S: Web.arising_recurs_iff (l.542) and Web.unceasing_iff (l.568): in a finite family, formations keep arising exactly when they keep ceasing, so kinds come and go. held_over_stretch (l.433): members holding at the end plus those that ceased equal those holding at the start plus those that came to be. B: Accretion.unceasing and never_ceases (l.589, l.592): ever new formations arise and none ceases while a level rises at every step, so more goes on after.

There is no Process S A.
places.reading: S: chosen_alike (l.126): with value reading exactly g's admission and what couples into g, histories alike through g's couplings are chosen alike, whatever the update and the choice. unchosen_beyond_coupling (l.138): a withheld part acting only beyond the coupling closure (given WithheldLevels, balance on the coupled conditions, and g within the closure) does not change the choice. pooled_unchosen_beyond (l.202) is the same for pooled folds. weighted (l.261) is the rule read from the counts.

places.multiplying: S: posterior_count_falls (l.390) and posterior_course_falls (l.399) step by CarrierCounts.select with byScore, so the counts become c·(s+κc) and o·(s+κo) (select is offspring per unit, in RuleCapture). Under choose, a count only rises by one per choice (l.227).

This is general in κc, κo, counts and schedule, on the CarrierCounts model. It is keeping one side or the other, not going on versus ending. B: Witness.counted_beats_score (l.451) against Witness.moved_locks_down (l.476).

The flow balances and is dissipative and dependent; the clearer is active and supported at every step on a resource renewed and fed from beyond by the source, while its take draws down the dweller's habitat, and the dweller is inactive from step 2 (undermines_within_renewal l.172). With the clearer's part withheld the dweller is admitted at every step; with it the dweller is lost beyond the clearer's dependence (admitted_without l.247, loses_beyond l.271, narrows l.262, centers_disagree l.322).

The ending is at a low level (the habitat at 0), not at the loss of something that gives.

places.place: ClosedCapture.lean: Unread, unread_course, identifiesAlike_iff_unread, courses_alike_iff_unread, join_course, lock_outlives_loss, turned_by_loss, both_reads, reading_absorbed, Drawn.pool_reads_iff, agreeing_stays, course_past, Thinned.kept_iff, Thinned.turned_iff
places.states: S: General laws on two-level Pace.paced loops. Where neither the next share nor the rule read reads what lies beyond the share (Unread), courses from starts alike in share and rule stay alike, exactly then (unread_course l.186, courses_alike_iff_unread l.202, identifiesAlike_iff_unread l.166). A locked loop outlives an accruing loss (lock_outlives_loss l.307); a reading that reads the loss turns (turned_by_loss l.291); a reading formed from the share is one rule read from the share (both_reads l.425, reading_absorbed l.455). On CarrierCounts: a pool of readers reads the share monotonically exactly when the carriers' reading is at least the others' (Drawn.pool_reads_iff l.612). With a mirrored late reading, the counts when the loss is read decide whether the lock is kept or turned for good (Thinned.kept_iff l.900, Thinned.turned_iff l.918). Built witnesses: Beyond, Proportional, Thinned.inTime and late.
places.moves: S: The only choice is the reading schedule reads : Nat → Bool, and laws hold along every schedule. identifiesAlike_iff_unread (l.166) and courses_alike_iff_unread (l.202) hold for all schedules exactly when Unread holds. goAlike_of_unread (l.147) uses Law.process (Pace.step f h reads). There is no choice among moves in a Process S A.
places.reading: S: Unread (l.131). identifiesAlike_iff_unread (l.166): share, rule and step count (loopPart) identify alike along every schedule exactly when Unread holds. turned_by_loss (l.291): where the rule read favours at no configuration whose loss is at least N and the loss accrues, the rule in force does not favour at the step after every reading step r with N ≤ b + r. Drawn.pool_reads_iff (l.612): the pool reads the share monotonically exactly when the others' reading is at most the carriers' reading.
places.share: S: lock_outlives_loss (l.307) assumes Raises, ReadsShare and a Locked start. Drawn.pool (l.558) sets the rule again from the readers counted by the population's share. Drawn.through_locks (l.646): readers formed monotonically from the share, every one reading favourably, lock every course from the step after its second reading step. Thinned.kept_iff (l.900): the lock is kept for good exactly when carriers are at least as many as others at the reading step.
places.level: S: Accrues (l.273). loss_grows (l.277): the loss at step t is at least its start plus t. lock_outlives_loss (l.307): the loss passes every bound while the course stays locked. turned_by_loss (l.291): the rule read depends on the loss reaching N. The loss grows; no stock runs down with what comes back depending on what is left.
places.giving: N: Not found. What lies beyond is a coordinate b stepped by a function fB handed in, not a going-on of the model.
places.multiplying: S: Drawn.through_locks (l.646) and Drawn.pool_not_rising (l.657) are stated over paced select, and CarrierCounts.select multiplies each kind by its offspring per unit. B: Beyond.closed_locked (l.365), Beyond.open_falls (l.375), Thinned.inTime_turned (l.960) and Thinned.late_kept (l.977) run join select.
places.no_return: S: Concluded from Raises, ReadsShare, upper and a Locked start. lock_outlives_loss (l.307): locked at every step while the loss passes every bound. agreeing_stays (l.765): from a reading step where the rule in force and the rule read both favour, the course is locked for good. Thinned.read_late_kept (l.830): kept for good. Thinned.read_in_time_turns (l.861): locked the other way for good. The irreversibility is of the lock, not at a low level and not at the loss of a giver.
places.both_outcomes: S: Thinned.kept_iff (l.900): with the late reading the mirror of the carriers' and the rule in force favouring, the course is locked at every later step exactly when carriers ≥ others at the reading step. Thinned.turned_iff (l.918): with the rule in force disfavouring, the course is turned for good exactly when carriers ≤ others. Both are general in fB, counts and step, on CarrierCounts. courses_alike_iff_unread (l.202) is general. B: Thinned.inTime_turned (l.960) against Thinned.late_kept (l.977), the same loss read in time or late. Beyond.closed_locked (l.365) against Beyond.open_turned (l.385).
places.comparison: S: unread_course (l.186): two courses from starts alike in share and rule keep the same share and rule at every step. join_course (l.248): the joined law runs share and rule exactly as the share's law alone. course_past (l.735): two readings agreeing at every configuration with loss ≥ N give one course from a start past N. Drawn.pool_mono (l.578): a share not lower gives a pool not lower.
places.rank: S: Bounds on when locking or turning occurs, not ending. turned_by_loss (l.291): not favouring at the step after any reading step r with N ≤ b + r. readers_uniform_locks (l.470) and Drawn.through_locks (l.646): locked from the step after the second reading step. N: no falling variant or drain.
places.closed_region: S: lock_outlives_loss (l.307), readers_not_below (l.438) and agreeing_stays (l.765): the Locked region is closed under every step and neither share, rule nor reading falls below where it was. reading_absorbed (l.455): a change of reading with a rule that still favours is absorbed at the next reading step.
places.forms_change: N: Not found. reading_absorbed (l.455) and Proportional.reform_absorbed (l.510) show a changed reading absorbed back, not a going-on continuing while forms change.
places.how_read: Every statement and docstring read, in two parts, lines 1–995. All fourteen answered from statements, with witnesses marked B. Definitions of Raises, ReadsShare, Locked, CarrierCounts and select were checked in RuleCapture.lean.

places.place: Closing.lean: strengthsBefore, couples_before_iff, onLoop_iff_formed, onLoop_succ_iff, forms_by_closing, responds_to_own_level, carried_before, carried_le_polynomial_before, ReadsBefore, formedCourse_eq_carried, Closing.Onset, Closing.Threshold
places.states: S: General laws for the carrying exchange (the CouplesAt, OnLoop and carried notions of Remainder and Loops). The loops a world has are exactly the loops formed by some step (onLoop_iff_formed l.178). The loops formed by T+1 are those formed by T plus those closed by a coupling acting at T (onLoop_succ_iff l.307, forms_by_closing l.332). Before a loop forms upstream, the carried amount is at most polynomial (carried_le_polynomial_before l.399). With strengths read from the levels so far, the course is the carried amount of the strengths it reads (formedCourse_eq_carried l.527). Built witnesses Onset (l.413) and Threshold (l.554): a loop forming at T or at θ, unforeseen from the amounts before.
places.moves: N: No choice among moves.
places.reading: S: ReadsBefore (l.492): strengths at each step depend only on the levels up to that step. formedCourse_eq_carried (l.527): the course the law with read strengths generates is the carried amount of those strengths. B: Threshold.reading (l.558): the exchange responds to the level once it reaches θ. Threshold.forms (l.650): the loop forms at step θ, so the registered level decides when it forms.
places.level: S: carried_le_polynomial_before (l.399): with every condition listed, starting gaps ≤ D and inflow ≤ M, and no loop formed by T upstream of c, the carried amount at c up to T is ≤ D · orderSum M n t. These amounts grow. N: no level that runs down with what comes back depending on what is left.
places.giving: N: Couplings are supplied strength functions (k, or κ read off the course). The account says the read strengths are supplied. No giver is a going-on that can be lost.
places.multiplying: B: Onset.amount_after (l.451): the amount is D·2^r after the loop forms. Threshold.level_after (l.617): level + 1 doubles at every step from θ. These are amounts doubling, not units leaving units.
places.no_return: S: couples_before_mono (l.127): couplings formed by a step stay formed by every later step, and onLoop_succ_iff keeps the earlier loops. This monotonicity is by the definition of strengthsBefore. N: no point of no return of a going-on. The account points to Remainder for loops dissolving.
places.both_outcomes: N: No going on versus ending, or keeping versus losing. onLoop_succ_iff (l.307) is an exactly-when for which loops are formed by a step.
places.comparison: S: carried_before (l.367): the carried amount up to T is the same under strengthsBefore T k as under k. OnLoop.lift and Upstream.lift (l.152, l.156): loops and upstream carry to strengths with more couplings. B: Onset.unforeseen (l.477) and Threshold.unforeseen (l.662): a loop forming at T and one forming at any later T' carry the same amounts up to T.
places.rank: N: No ending within a bound and no falling variant. carried_le_polynomial_before (l.399) is an upper bound on growth before a loop forms.
places.closed_region: N: Not found.
places.forms_change: S: onLoop_succ_iff (l.307), forms_by_closing (l.332) and responds_to_own_level (l.343): loops come to be at the step a coupling closes a chain, within the unfolding. B: Threshold.forms (l.650) and Threshold.not_formed (l.633): a loop read off the course forms when the level reaches θ, and the course grows geometrically after (Threshold.level_after l.617).

places.place: CodeAcquisition.lean: acquired_exact, acquired_every_expression, primitives_no_exact, train, trainProcess, step_stock, step_rests_when_short, step_code_transfers, step_then_execute, installed_without_execution
places.states: B: One built finite model: expressions from two atoms, and codes giving atom values and a join order. The code read off three probes is the code wherever its primitives differ (acquired_exact l.110, acquired_every_expression l.120); no reading of the primitives alone is exact for the order (primitives_no_exact l.275). Training is a process of the spine (trainProcess l.345): a step draws seven units from the learner's stock, installs the code and appends records, and leaves a learner with stock below seven as it was (step_stock l.361, step_installs l.356, step_rests_when_short l.366).
places.moves: S: trainProcess : Process Learner Code (l.345), where the move c trains under c. step_code_transfers (l.372): every move c with stock ≥ 7 and c.first ≠ c.second installs acquire (observe c), which evaluates every expression as c does. step_rests_when_short (l.366): every move leaves a learner with stock < 7 unchanged.
places.reading: S: observe (l.100) and acquire (l.103). acquired_exact (l.110): the code read off the probes is the code where its primitives differ. primitives_not_lumped (l.268) and primitives_no_exact (l.275): read through the primitives alone, the order is not lumped and no answer is exact (PartialReadout). step_evidence (l.378): from no records, the step's records read back as the code's probes. places.level: S: The learner's stock. step_stock (l.361): a covered step draws seven. step_rests_when_short (l.366): with stock < 7 the step changes nothing. step_then_execute (l.384): execution draws operationDraw, and what is left plus both draws equals the stock before. Whether training or execution can happen depends on the stock left. B: installed_without_execution (l.398): from 7 the code is installed but the novel expression cannot be executed.
places.giving: N: Not found. Nothing gives to the stock; it is a number in the Learner.
places.cost: S: Training costs the learner its own stock. training_stock and step_stock (l.230, l.361): (train c s).stock + 7 = s.stock. trained_execution_stock (l.252): execution draws operationDraw from what is left. B: installed_not_executed (l.299).
places.no_return: S: step_rests_when_short (l.366): a learner with stock < 7 is left as it was by any move. Since no step raises the stock, short is not left, but this is stated only per step, not as a law over runs. It is at a low level (the stock), not at the loss of a giver.
places.both_outcomes: S: train_of_le (l.213) and training_short (l.235): for stock ≥ 7 the code is installed and seven are drawn; for stock < 7 the learner is unchanged. These are the two cases of one built model. B: novel_after_step (l.392, from 11, executes with nothing left) against installed_without_execution (l.398, from 7).

B: nonuniform_agrees_on_probes (l.327) and nonuniform_fails_transfer (l.332): a law agreeing on the probes differs on the novel expression.

places.states: For every law T and every map σ with no fixed point (Diagonal.Moves Eq σ), if T commutes with σ then the runs of T from x and from σ x are never at one configuration at the same step (Commutes.apart, l. 81), so merging them requires that T not commute (Commutes.breaks, l. 86). For processes, a σ that carries every step to a step carries reach, returning and (under an exchange) junctures, and gives each run a mirror run that is never at the same configuration. All laws are general; the Hexagram instance is stated elsewhere.
places.moves: S: Branching.Symmetric (l. 150) for Process S A: σ carries every step x a y to the step σ x a σ y. Symmetric.reach (l. 152), Symmetric.returns (l. 155) and Symmetric.juncture (l. 159) carry these properties to images. Branching.mirror (l. 167) maps every run to a run, and mirror_apart (l. 171) says it is never at the same configuration as that run at the same step, for every run. The other laws are of a deterministic law T.
places.reading: S: Commutes.pairs_lumped (l. 122): under an exchange σ, if a naming q names x and σ x alike and nothing else with x, the law read through q goes alike (Learning.Lumped q (q ∘ T)). Commutes.pairs_goAlike (l. 132) is the same as GoAlike (process T) q.

The point of no return (loss of reach to a configuration) is a premise carried, not concluded, and it is of a configuration, not of something that gives.
places.both_outcomes: N: no dichotomy is stated. A juncture holds both a keeping step and a losing step at one configuration, but here it appears only as a carried premise (l. 159).

Symmetric.reach (l. 152), returns (l. 155) and juncture (l. 159) carry reach, returning and junctures from x to σ x. law_symmetric (l. 176): a commuting law is a symmetric process. Commutes.returns_paired (l. 186): returning carries over to the image.

places.forms_change: S: Commutes.self_apart (l. 139): for f with no fixed point, the run of f never rests (state n+1 ≠ state n at every n), so the run goes on while its configuration changes at every step. Commutes.paired_halfway (l. 112): under an exchange, if the run reaches σ x at step k, every state has its image k steps on and x is had again at 2k, an alternation. Commutes.halfway_returns (l. 191): such a course returns.

Every order except the lag-for-each-admission one ranks a course above another only where it keeps what the other keeps (l. 545-576). Further general laws: parts read through a description lift exactly when the configurations it identifies match parts (liftsFromEach_iff, l. 598), and nested plans are realized at a description exactly when they are realized at every configuration it describes (JointPlan.realizes_image_iff, l. 645; plans_lift_iff, l. 679). JointPlan.realizes_image_iff (l. 645): with matching and correct leaf reading, π realizes a plan exactly when every configuration π describes does. places.states: General laws: on a relation without cycles, the returning elements are exactly the sinks (returnsAlong_iff_sink, l. 106). On a net going forward in time, the root's condition «续无外» holds exactly when everything later is reached from each center and nothing else lies at or before the center's step («续无外当且仅当后与独», l. 168). Held de se at every occurrence of a flow, the condition from some step on holds exactly when the flow is mutually dependent in time (l. 430), and the condition over every later step holds exactly when every formation affects every other at the next step (l. 441). Built witnesses: TwoSources, Recurring, RingOfThree, Drawing, LatePair.
places.moves: N: a flow's present/take/give are supplied functions. StepInTime (l. 264) is a relation on occurrences with no choice among steps.
places.reading: S: datedOwnClosure (l. 386) makes a standpoint's significance in time whatever lies within its center's closure along the relation. unrestrictedEventually_iff_mutuallyDependentInTime (l. 430) says when that significance reaches every formation from some step on. D: the account (l. 82) calls reading significance as own closure 'itself a reading'. There is no observation class and no rule made from what is registered.
places.level: B: LatePair.web (l. 682): levels of 1 at steps 0 and 1 and 0 after, supplied, not run down by a law. Flow.AffectsBefore (l. 259) uses positive take or give from a condition. D: the account (l. 71-76) cites Flow.member_after_never_overdrew (never overdrawing a short stock) and says it now stands in Becoming.PersistingChoices, not in this module. N: no law in this module of a level running down with return depending on what is left.
places.giving: N: exchanges are supplied functions of the flow. B: Drawing.lapses (l. 637): after the first step nothing is exchanged, so mutual dependence in time lapses. The ceasing is supplied, not derived.
places.cost: N. D: the account (l. 81) notes that exchanging counts taking as well as giving, so mutual dependence in time includes mutual drain.
places.no_return: S: MutuallyDependentFrom.earlier (l. 354): mutual dependence in time from step t holds from every earlier step. The module does not state the contrapositive, that once it fails from a step it fails from every later one; that follows. B: Drawing.lapses (l. 637): it holds from step 0 and not from step 1. S: not_returnsAlong_stepInTime (l. 306): no occurrence returns along the step in time; WithinTime.le (l. 347): nothing earlier is reached. Both are concluded, about time order, not the loss of something that gives.
places.both_outcomes: S: unrestrictedEventually_iff_mutuallyDependentInTime (l. 430) and unrestrictedAfter_iff_coupledEachStep (l. 441) say exactly when a condition holds, for every flow. These are not dichotomies of going on and ending. B: LatePair.apart (l. 723): mutually dependent, yet mutually dependent in time from no step.
places.comparison: S: WithinTime.withinReach (l. 324): what lies within an occurrence's closure in time lies within its formation's reach closure. MutuallyDependentFrom.mutuallyDependent (l. 362): dated mutual dependence from any step gives undated mutual dependence; the converse fails (B: LatePair.apart, l. 723). «续无外则续无外于后» (l. 191): the root's condition gives the condition over what comes after.
places.rank: N: «及则后» (l. 152) says reach along a forward net goes to later times, but no bound on ending is stated.
places.closed_region: N: closures in time (WithinTime, l. 268) and sinks (returnsAlong_of_sink, l. 98) are stated, but no invariant, kernel or largest closed region.
places.forms_change: N: in every witness the present formations are fixed lists. S: withinTime_onward (l. 334): a formation's continuation lies within its own closure in time at every later step. B: Recurring.inTime (l. 508), where two formations exchange at every step, and RingOfThree.apart (l. 607) go on with the same formations.

places.place: ConditionalWeights.lean: restrict, mass_restrict, mass_split, restrict_two_ways, posterior_single, posterior_le_iff, share_meetsEach, fallsWithin_bound, fallsWithin_share, record_fallsWithin, record_share, record_bound, Witness.within_exceeds_end, Witness.record_reverses
places.states: The module states, in general for every natural weighting on a listed domain, the counting form of conditioning: a weighting restricted to a record, the law of total weight, Bayes's rule as cross-multiplied shares, the posterior of a generative model, and products of shares over independent parts and independent steps. For the two-valued courses of Typicality with weights p and q, in general in p, q, m and n, it bounds the weight and share of courses in which a level standing m above a need reaches it within n steps, and states that a record of the earlier steps bears on this only through the margin it shows and the steps it leaves.
places.moves: N: no choice among steps and no law about what a choice keeps. Every course of the listed moves is weighed (independentWeight, l. 699; courses moves all n in mass_meetsEach, l. 712); none is chosen.
places.reading: S: `restrict` (l. 297), with `mass_restrict` (l. 302): under the weighting restricted to a Boolean record, an event weighs what the courses meeting both the event and the record weigh. `posterior_le_iff` (l. 588): with the record's weight positive, two classes of hypotheses compare after the record exactly as their prior weights times the record's weights under them, summed. `record_share` (l. 1069): for a record of the earliest k steps that, on every course agreeing with it, leaves the level m' above the need without having reached it, the share of courses reaching the need within the horizon is the same ratio as the share reaching it from m' over the n steps left. So the margin the record shows decides the exit share. B: `Witness.record_reverses` (l. 1182): a record turns the order of two hypotheses (15 against 5 becomes 3 against 5).
places.share: S: `Share` (l. 345) and `share` (l. 416): an event's mass out of the whole mass, kept as two naturals and compared by cross-multiplication. Laws are stated of it (share_le_of_included l. 420, share_product l. 497, posterior_single l. 658, fallsWithin_share l. 890). N: no rule or favouring is set again from a share; no step's weighting is formed from a share.
places.level: S: `fallsTo` (l. 796) and `fallsWithin` (l. 839): a level m above a need, raised q by each one and lowered p by each zero, ends at or below the need, or reaches it at some step. `fallsWithin_bound` (l. 869): the courses of n steps that reach it at some step weigh, times m·m, at most n·p·q·(p+q)^n. `fallsTo_succ` (l. 801): falling below the need is reaching it from m+1. N: what comes back does not depend on what is left; rises and falls come from independent step weights p and q whatever the level.
places.giving: N: the rise q on each one is a fixed term of the definition, not a going-on of the model that can be lost. D: the Correspondence paragraph of the opening says persisting longer needs a giving that reads the level. No statement has one.
places.no_return: N: no irreversibility. B: `Witness.within_exceeds_end` (l. 1145): with weights 1 and 1 over two steps, a level one above the need reaches it at some step on two of four courses but ends below it on only one, because a course can fall and recover.
places.both_outcomes: N: no exactly-when of going on and ending. The exit is only bounded from above (fallsWithin_bound l. 869, fallsWithin_share l. 890). D: the opening says the bound is void from n = m·m/(p·q) and that a balanced walk recurs, 'not proved here'.
places.comparison: S: `restrict_two_ways` (l. 440): restricting by the record and then sharing the hypothesis gives the same ratio as restricting by the hypothesis and then sharing the record. `mass_record` (l. 1020) and `record_fallsWithin` (l. 1056): the courses of k+n steps that agree with a record and meet an event weigh the record's weight times the weight, over n steps, of the event the later steps carry. `fallsTo_append` (l. 982) and `fallsWithin_append` (l. 995): after a record showing margin m', reaching the need from m equals reaching it from m' over the later steps, which carries the exit from one start to another. `share_le_of_included` (l. 420): a wider event has no smaller share.
places.rank: N: no variant falls and no ending within a bound. S, a bound within a horizon only: `fallsWithin_share` (l. 890): within n steps the exit takes at most n·p·q over m·m of the weight. That bounds weight, not an ending.
places.closed_region: N
places.forms_change: N

places.states: The module states, in general, that the process of a revision rule that does not read the failure answers every failure exactly where every step reporting no failure lands on a plan contacting every address. places.place: Counting.lean: counting_under, counting_binds_iff, counting_binds_jointly, enclosure_bounds_change, finite_change_bound_iff, enclosed_iff_finite_counting_under, binding_counting_under, binding_contingent, EnclosedQueue.empty_stays, lpo_of_finite_ends
places.states: The module states what the eight premises, and each of their 256 selections, add to the law of counting: a property of the census counts (n active, c ceasing, a arising) holds of every census of every world meeting the selection exactly when it holds of every Tally meeting added conditions. These conditions are that nothing arises across a step at which nothing is active, a change bound from the first step under enclosure or finiteness, and that something is active or arises where premises bind. The laws are general, stated for every World, and each is witnessed by built queues and rings (queue, openQueue, enclosedQueue, finiteQueue, onceClosedQueue, lossyQueue, relayQueue, ring, relayRing, lossyRing, exchangingRing, sheddingQueue).
places.moves: N: no process with a choice among steps, policy or allowed set was found in any statement. Each World has one flow and one web. The selection S : Premise -> Bool (World.Meets S, BindsCounting l. 743, BoundsChange l. 1652) is a choice of which premises hold, not of moves.
places.reading: S: the counts of a census (Web.Census alive; CensusMarksHold Q; CountsHold) are what every law speaks of. Pointwise Q (used by counting_free l. 308, counting_under l. 853 and every other law) restricts to properties of the counts that respect their values at each step. counting_under (l. 853) states that what can be known of the counts under a selection is exactly the tally plus, where BindsCounting S holds, 0 < a t -> 0 < n t. N: no rule or selection is set from what is counted, and nothing registered decides a later step.
places.share: N: the counts n, c, a are numbers of relata active, ceasing and arising, not shares of one kind among several, and no rule or favouring is set from them.
places.level: S: `enclosure_bounds_change` (l. 907): in a world with a census whose relata are embodied, a balanced, dissipative flow and every step from T on enclosed, ChangeBound T (stock (alive T) T) holds. That is, for t >= T the number active plus the number of steps since T at which something ceased or arose is at most the total standing at T (the counted form is `enclosure_bounds_change_counted`, l. 932). Its docstring says the premises make what stands run down across those steps. B: `EnclosedQueue.store` (l. 983) is B less one for each step at which something ceased or arose, and `EnclosedQueue.store_succ_le` (l. 4524) states the store never grows. `enclosedQueue_stock` (l. 1177) states that what stands is at most the store, and equals it while the queue is not empty. What can still change is bounded by what is left, but no statement gives a return as a function of the level.
places.giving: S: `active_of_coming_jointly` (l. 357): where the flow balances, only active relata give (Acting) and whatever arises is embodied, something coming to be across a step under a census needs something active at that step. `active_of_coming_taking` (l. 368) gives the same from balance, Taking, Dissipative and Embodied, whoever gives. `active_of_coming_enclosed` (l. 953) gives it at an enclosed step from balance, dissipation and embodiment. So what gives to arising is itself a relatum of the world, one counted in the census and able to cease. `counting_binds_jointly` (l. 333) states that this is no law of tallies: Queue.lone is counted by a queue meeting every premise but embodiment, and by one meeting every premise but balance. In the witnesses the giver is the queue's front (openQueue l. 477, enclosedQueue l. 1139), a member that leaves.
places.cost: B: in the enclosed queue the front holds the store beyond one per member, and `enclosedQueue_dissipatesOn` (l. 1199) states that where something joins or leaves, what stands falls by one, so the front takes more than it gives. `onceClosedQueue_exceeds` (l. 2488): across T the front, standing E more, takes from the span more than it gives. `LossyQueue.lost` (l. 2800) and `lossyQueue` (l. 2833): across U the front loses one unit more from itself, which no standing records. `sheddingQueue_exceeds` (l. 4620): the front sheds its spare unit across T. S, partly: `enclosure_bounds_change` (l. 907) charges each change to the total standing of the closed family, not to a particular giver. N: no general statement charges giving to the one that gives.
places.multiplying: N: no law of the step fixes how many arise per active relatum; under every law the arising count a is free within a Tally and the added conditions. S, partly: `active_of_coming_jointly` (l. 357) requires an active relatum at any step across which something arises. `binding_joint_iff` (l. 3377) states that something arises across a step at which something is active exactly where embodiment is selected and either the selection binds counting or only active relata giving and bounded transmission are selected; its docstring says what arises then descends from a relatum active at the step. No units leaving units by a rate.
places.no_return: S, in two pieces, with no single world-level theorem joining them. (a) Concluded for every census of every world meeting a selection that binds counting (`counting_under_sound` l. 809, `counting_binds_iff` l. 861, `CountsOf.company_binding` l. 2734): 0 < a t -> 0 < n t. (b) `EnclosedQueue.empty_stays` (l. 1057), stated for any tally: with Tally n c a and the premise 0 < a t -> 0 < n t at t, n t = 0 gives n (t+1) = 0. Together they say that once no relatum is active (the loss of everything that gives), nothing is active again. That is concluded from the premises of balance, embodiment and acting (or taking with dissipation). S: `lpo_of_finite_ends` (l. 1559): if every finite world meeting the eight with decided activity had a step after which nothing arises, LPO would hold. `lpo_of_census_ends` (l. 5085): the same for a step after which nothing ceases or arises, in every world with a change bound and the company condition. So an end of arising is not concluded. The irreversibility is at the loss of what gives, the active relata.
places.both_outcomes: B: `binding_contingent` (l. 2638): under all eight premises with every premise binding, `hatch` does not have ArisingRecurs, while onceClosedQueue (fun _ => 1) (fun _ => 1) 0 2 has ArisingRecurs and CeasingRecurs. Both outcomes are shown, but in two built models, not as an exactly-when for one model. S, over selections rather than one model: `finite_change_bound_iff` (l. 2196): a change bound from the first step is a law of counting in finite worlds under S exactly when S selects balance, embodiment and dissipation; otherwise a ring with one member replaced at every step is counted and its change recurs. `enclosed_change_bound_iff` (l. 1753) states the same in worlds enclosed from some step on, with a count growing by one at each step as the counter-witness. N: no exactly-when of going on and ending for one model.
places.comparison: S: `enclosed_iff_finite_counting` (l. 1514): under the eight premises, worlds enclosed from some step on and finite worlds have the same laws of counting. `enclosed_iff_finite_counting_under` (l. 2285) and `enclosed_iff_finite_tally` (l. 2230): the two classes have the same laws under S exactly when BoundsChange S and BindsCounting S both hold. `Premised.saturated` (l. 2702): saturating a world's web keeps every premise and makes activity needing support and bounded transmission hold where levels are bounded; this carries the premises from w to w.saturated. B: `Ring.counts` (l. 1937): a ring seating a queue counts what the queue counts. `closing_flows` (l. 1607): from T on, the closing queue's flow is the enclosed queue's. N: no stepwise simulation or order kept by the step between two processes.
places.rank: S: `enclosure_bounds_change` (l. 907), with its counted form `enclosure_bounds_change_counted` (l. 932): from T on, the count plus the number of change steps since T stays within the standing at T. This is the corollary of Flow.runsDown_change_bound: standing runs down at each change step, so change is bounded. `enclosed_counting` (l. 1303) and `finite_counting` (l. 1504) make a change bound from the first step a law under the eight premises, with enclosure from some step on or in finite worlds. `replaced_attains` (l. 1544) shows the bound attained in a built finite queue. The bound limits the number of change steps, but no step of ending is given (`lpo_of_finite_ends`, l. 1559).
places.closed_region: S: closed families across a step (Flow.ClosedAt, Flow.Enclosed). `still_enclosed` (l. 1656): where nothing takes part, every step is enclosed. `enclosed_binds_counting` (l. 715): at an enclosed step, balance, dissipation and embodiment give that nothing arises if nothing is active. S, at tally level: `EnclosedQueue.empty_stays` (l. 1057): emptiness is kept across a step under the company condition, an invariant. B: `enclosedQueue_enclosed` (l. 1264) and `EnclosedQueue.closed` (l. 1119): each step of the enclosed queue is enclosed by its span. `Queue.lone_settles` (l. 1967): from step 1 on the lone relatum is all there is and nothing changes. N: no largest closed region, kernel or fixed point of a step map.
places.forms_change: B: `binding_contingent` (l. 2638): in onceClosedQueue (fun _ => 1) (fun _ => 1) 0 2, one member replaces another at every step, one member is always active, and arising and ceasing recur, with every premise binding. `replaced` (l. 1523) and `replaced_attains` (l. 1544): one member replaced across the first step. The relay witnesses `relayQueue` (l. 3031) and `relayRing` (l. 3657) hand one of two units on to a ground relatum or place, which comes to stand. S, the limit on this: `finite_change_bound_iff` (l. 2196): in finite worlds, endless one-for-one replacement is excluded exactly when balance, embodiment and dissipation are selected. N: no statement in which more can go on after (a widening).
places.how_read: All fourteen were answered from statements or built cases, partly with docstrings (giving and level cite docstrings beside statements); none is D only and none is U. I read the whole module (all statements and docstrings, l. 1-5110), proof bodies only in part.

places.place: CoupledDrawers.lean: drains_below, drain_perfect, kept_above, keeping_perfect, kept_levels, gated_threshold, one_keeps_several_drain, AtOnce.drain_perfect_iff, AtOnce.drain_perfect_iff_reach, AtOnce.unpivotal_drain_perfect, AtOnce.Shores.drain_perfect, perfect_uncoupled
places.states: The module states drawers that draw from one level over a finite horizon, each paid c for every step at which what all leave meets a need m. Its laws are general in the law G of what stands next: below the need (c < m) every perfect profile of two or more drawers in turn leaves nothing at every step, and above it (m < c), under three gate premises on G, every perfect profile keeps exactly the need. A built family (gatedRenewal, Shores) shows the threshold is the need itself, that one drawer keeps where several drain, and that drawing at once without a pivotal drawer the drain is perfect at every rate.
places.moves: S: `Revises`/`Perfect` (l. 119, l. 126): each drawer's rule, a function of the step and of the amount it is given, is a best response among leaving anything from its floor to all of it, over the steps that remain. `drains_below` (l. 367): with 1 < k, no floor, 0 < m and c < m, every perfect profile has every drawer leave nothing at every step t < N, whatever G is. `kept_above` (l. 582): under `gate`, `holds` and `regrows`, with m < c, every perfect profile has every drawer leave `keep m a`. `drain_perfect` (l. 386) and `keeping_perfect` (l. 603) say the drain is perfect where c ≤ m and keeping is perfect where m ≤ c. At once: `AtOnce.Perfect` (l. 825). This is not a `Process S A`.
places.reading: N: there is no observation or class of things read alike. The nearest is `stepCoupling` (l. 66): the reward counts only whether what is left b meets m (c if m ≤ b, else 0).
places.share: N: in AtOnce a drawer draws from its `portion d t z` (handed in; built as `Shores.shore p`, l. 1003), but no rule or favouring is set again from a share.
places.level: S: the level z steps by a supplied G of what all leave (`InTurn.levels`, used in `kept_levels` l. 639). The gate premises (l. 433) say that below the need what stands next is below it, that at or above the need it meets it, and `regrows`: G t 0 + m ≤ G t m. `gatedRenewal m q` (l. 656) leaves an amount below m as it is and adds q at or above m, so what comes back depends on what is left. `kept_levels` (l. 639): from a start at least m, under all-keep and `holds`, the level meets m at every step to the horizon, and exactly m is left at each step.
places.giving: N: what renews the level is G, a function handed in (built: `gatedRenewal`, identity in Shores). The drawers are indices, not going-ons that can be lost.
places.cost: S: a drawer's worth is what it draws now (a - b) plus later rewards, so leaving costs the drawer itself. `leaves_nothing` (l. 209): where c < m is all that leaving brings, a best response leaves nothing. The `drains_at` docstring (l. 322) says the last drawer's keeping brings it c against the m it leaves. `leaves_need` (l. 230): where W + m < V, a best response leaves exactly `keep m a`.
places.no_return: S, premise and conclusion: `gate` (l. 433, a premise on G) says that below the need what stands next stays below it. Concluded: `AtOnce.drained_unmet` (l. 978) says that under the drain profile no positive need is met at any step. `Shores.drain_perfect` (l. 1026) has the drain perfect at every rate with the need met at no step, though both drawers leaving all would leave p + p ≥ m. The loss is at a low level (the amount below m), not the loss of something that gives.
places.both_outcomes: S: `gated_threshold` (l. 774): on `gatedRenewal m q` for every q, with 1 < k and 0 < m, over every horizon: c < m makes every perfect profile drain at every step; c ≤ m makes the drain perfect; m ≤ c makes keeping perfect; m < c makes every perfect profile keep exactly the need, met at every step from a start at least m. Built family, general in k and N. General over G under the gate: `drains_below` (l. 367) together with `kept_above` (l. 582). `AtOnce.drain_perfect_iff` (l. 895, general): the drain is perfect exactly where no drawer alone gains from its reward more than it leaves. `drain_perfect_iff_reach` (l. 948): where what is left returns nothing, the drain is perfect exactly where c ≤ m wherever a portion reaches m. `one_keeps_several_drain` (l. 692, built): one drawer keeps the need at the first of two steps, while every perfect profile of two or more drawers leaves nothing.

places.states: General laws on any flow L : Flow F C with a web W, with the premises balance (Balances) and dissipation (DissipatesOn or Dissipative). A family dissipated on falls each step by at least the number of its takers, the takers over all later steps number at most its stock, and taking from it does not recur. So under dissipation, recurring taking (more without end, unceasing arising, or maintenance) leaves no finite family closed from any step on, and where the family is enclosed around it draws in from beyond; the same holds for rising and coming to stand, and a rise comes with a fall. Built: Frontier, Rooted and Lone meet the premises, Spray is dissipative vacuously, and the flows of Becoming.Flow are not dissipative.
places.moves: N: no Process or choice. The flows are given (present, take, give).
places.reading: N: not found.
places.share: N: `Flow.takers cs t` counts the formations taking from a family, and this count bounds the stock's fall (`Balances.runs_down`, l. 387). No rule or favouring is set again from a share.
places.level: S: `Balances.runs_down` (l. 387): with `L.Balances W` and `L.DissipatesOn cs t`, W.stock cs (t+1) + L.takers cs t ≤ W.stock cs t. `Balances.takers_within` (l. 406): dissipated on from S, the stock at S+N plus all takers over the stretch is at most the stock at S, so how much taking can still come depends on the stock left. `BalancesOn.comes_from_standing` (l. 378): a member comes to stand only where the family stood at something before.
places.giving: S: givers are formations present in the flow. `DissipatesOn.takes_of_gives` (l. 284): a formation present that gives to a family dissipated on takes from it. `taking_draws_in` (l. 587): with balance, dissipation, a distinct family enclosed around from T₀ and recurring takers, at arbitrarily late steps the family is not Inward, so some formation gives to it and takes from beyond. N: that a giver can be lost is not stated. B: `Frontier.gives_without_taking` (l. 1025): the source gives the pool while taking nothing from it, burning fuel instead.
places.cost: S: `Dissipative.gives_less` (l. 309): under dissipation, over a distinct family closed across a step, a formation that gives takes more than it gives. `Dissipative.giving_needs_uptake` (l. 316): across an enclosed step, a formation that gives takes from some condition. The cost is uptake by the giver, not its own standing drawn on (that is N).
places.multiplying: B: `Frontier.flow` (l. 890) and `Frontier.more` (l. 979): one grower arises at each step and t growers take from the pool at step t. `Rooted.rooted` (l. 1127): with growers depending on the pool, the arising is unceasing (web.Unceasing). The count changes by definition of the built flow; no units leave units.
places.no_return: S, concluded from premises: `Balances.taking_not_recurring` (l. 427): balanced and dissipated on from some step T, it is not the case that formations take from the family at arbitrarily late steps. `rising_not_recurring_on` (l. 638) and `standing_not_recurring_on` (l. 644) state the same for rising and coming to stand. `Dissipative.finite_taking_not_recurring` (l. 461): if finitely many conditions are all there is, taking never recurs. This concerns the family's stock (a low level). No explicit step after which none occurs is named.
places.both_outcomes: N: no exactly-when. `Dissipative.opens` (l. 452) is one direction: recurring taking implies no finite family containing it is closed from any step on. B, a contrast across built flows: `witnesses_not_dissipative` (l. 1369) shows the expansion, cycle, pulse, steady, repeated and oscillation flows of Becoming.Flow and Becoming.Population are not dissipative, while Frontier (`frontier` l. 985) and Lone (`frontier` l. 1217) are dissipative and open.
places.comparison: S: `takers_pos_of_sub` (l. 433): a formation taking from a family takes from every family containing it (closed upward). `taking_not_recurring_within` (l. 443): non-recurrence carries from a containing family dissipated on. `Enclosed.around` (l. 508): with decidable equality, enclosed implies enclosed around every family; `Enclosed.around_not_not` (l. 518) is the form without decision.
places.rank: S: `BalancesOn.runs_down` (l. 327) and `Balances.runs_down` (l. 387): the stock falls each step by at least the number of takers. `takers_within_on` (l. 394) and `Balances.takers_within` (l. 406): the total takers over any later stretch are bounded by the stock at its start. This is a drain whose variant is the stock.
places.closed_region: S, of families closed in exchange, not of regions of configurations: `ClosedAt` (l. 237), `Enclosed` (l. 253), `Around` (l. 259). `Dissipative.opens` (l. 452) and `More.opens` (l. 486): under dissipation, recurring taking leaves no finite distinct family closed from any step on. N: no invariant region of states.
places.forms_change: S: `More.opens` (l. 486) and `opens_of_arising` (l. 492): under dissipation, more without end, or unceasing arising of formations that take, needs exchange beyond every finite family at arbitrarily late steps. B: `Frontier.frontier` (l. 985) and `Rooted.rooted` (l. 1127): a fresh fuel is burnt and a new grower arises at each step, and every finite family containing the pool is open at arbitrarily late steps. B: `Lone.lone` (l. 1208) and `Lone.frontier` (l. 1217): keeping one eater fed, with nothing arising, also reaches beyond every finite family.

places.states: General laws with no premise. Under a determined law read through a map, in a world of N listed configurations, two configurations pass the same tests exactly when their futures through the map agree for N-1 steps; across two worlds of N and N' configurations the bound is N+N'-1 steps; and two laws read through maps are alike exactly when their futures agree at every step. Every history with at most N states is the course of a law on N configurations. Built frames show the depths are exact.
places.moves: S: `Law.labelled` (l. 119): a Frame with a single move at each configuration, named by the map's value. `Law.alikeTo_labelled_iff` (l. 124): two such frames are alike to depth k iff the futures through the maps agree for k steps. There is no choice among several moves.
places.reading: S: `Law.sameTests_iff_within` (l. 86): with `∀ s, s ∈ l`, SameTests (Law.frameBy next o) s s' iff o agrees along the two orbits for every n < l.length - 1. `Law.sameTests_iff_below_across` (l. 98) gives the same across two worlds with bound l.length + l'.length - 1. `Law.alike_iff_agree` (l. 74): Alike iff agreement at every step. What the map registers decides likeness and the tests.

places.giving: N: not found.
places.no_return: N: not found.
places.both_outcomes: N: no exactly-when of going on and ending, or of keeping and losing. The iffs here are of likeness and tests.
places.comparison: S: `Law.agree_bisimulation` (l. 57): agreeing at every step is a bisimulation between two laws read through maps. `Law.alike_iff_agree` (l. 74). `Law.sameTests_iff_below_across` (l. 98) carries tests between two worlds.
places.rank: N: no law of ending within a bound. S, a bound of another kind: `Law.sameTests_iff_within` (l. 86) bounds the depth of distinguishing by N-1, and `frameBy_within_exact` (l. 245), `frameBy_across_exact` (l. 222) and `labelled_across_exact` (l. 196) show by built frames that the bounds N-1 and N+N'-1 are exact.
places.closed_region: S: `Law.agree_bisimulation` (l. 57): the relation 'futures through the maps agree at every step' is a bisimulation, so it is closed under the steps of both laws.
places.forms_change: N: not found. `frameBy_within_exact` (l. 245) is built on a path of N places to a last one that stays, which is not a case of forms changing.

places.states: General laws of the scalar regime step RegimeMargin.step g H x = (x - H) + g (x - H) (draw taken first, giving from what is left) under a schedule of draws (underDraws): the inflow g 0 is a rest and is kept while every draw is at least it, leaving it needs a lower draw, a draw above every giving up to hi collapses every level up to hi to the inflow within x - H + 1 steps, and the draws before decide which of two levels a course is at under the same final draw. The laws are general over g, H, schedules and bounds; Loop is one built witness.
places.moves: N: no Process with moves, policy or allowed set. The schedule of draws Hs is a function handed in. Read as choices: inflow_kept (l. 74) holds for every schedule whose draws from T on are at least g 0, and history_decides (l. 149) is about one schedule, raised for T steps and then brought back.
places.reading: N: nothing in the module is a reading, an observation or a rule made from what is registered.
places.share: N: there is no share or fraction of kinds; the level is a single whole number.
places.level: S: `collapses` (l. 112): if g z < H for every z ≤ hi and x ≤ hi, then the orbit of RegimeMargin.step g H from x is g 0 at every n ≥ x - H + 1. The level is drawn down by H, and what comes back, g (x - H), depends on what is left (RegimeMargin.step, RegimeMargin l. 249; underDraws l. 50). `two_levels` (l. 129): with Meets g H y hi, Keeps g H hi, g 0 ≤ H and H + y ≤ x ≤ hi, the run from x never falls below x, and g 0 rests under the same draw.
places.giving: N: the giving g : Nat → Nat is a function handed in. It is not a unit or formation of the model that can be lost.
places.cost: N: no statement has a giving or keeping that costs the one who does it.
places.multiplying: N: there are no units leaving units and no kinds forming kinds.
places.no_return: S: `inflow_kept` (l. 74): a level at g 0 at step T, with every draw from T on at least g 0, is g 0 at every later step. `leaving_needs_a_lower_draw` (l. 85): a level at the inflow at T that is not the inflow at T + k had a draw below g 0 at some step between. `history_decides` (l. 149): after draws above every giving for T ≥ x - H' + 1 steps and then H ≥ g 0, the level is g 0 forever. These are concluded, from the premise that later draws stay at least g 0. They are at a low level (the inflow rest), not at the loss of something that gives. The account says leaving is not shown to be recovery.
places.both_outcomes: S: `history_decides` (l. 149) is a conjunction of two outcomes under the same later draw H for the same start x: under the raised-then-returned schedule the level is g 0 from T on, and under H all along it never falls below x. `histories_differ` (l. 162): with g 0 < x the first is strictly below the second at every step from T. `two_levels` (l. 129) gives a held level and an inflow rest under one draw. It is a dichotomy decided by history, not an exactly-when. B: `Loop.two_paths` (l. 247), `Loop.bounds` (l. 259).
places.comparison: S: `histories_differ` (l. 162) compares two histories from one start: the raised-and-returned level is strictly below the constant-draw level at every step from T. `underDraws_constant` (l. 136): a schedule equal to H up to T gives the run under H up to T. No law carries an order or simulation between two processes; RegimeMargin.Keeps (the step keeps levels up to hi) is a premise.
places.rank: S: `collapses` (l. 112) is an explicit deadline: under a draw above every giving up to hi, the level from x ≤ hi is the inflow from step x - H + 1 on (through RegimeMargin.Adjusted.taken_whole). `inflow_from` (l. 101): once the run is at or below H at step m, it is the inflow from m + 1. B: `Loop.bounds` (l. 259): under draw 4, every level up to 8 is 1 from step 9.
places.closed_region: S: `inflow_stays` (l. 66): with g 0 ≤ H, g 0 is a fixed point of the step. `inflow_kept` (l. 74): {g 0} is kept under any schedule of draws at least g 0. `two_levels` (l. 129) / RegimeMargin.holds: the band at or above x is never left, with Keeps g H hi a premise.
places.forms_change: N: no statement or built case has a going on that continues while what is present changes, or that widens. The account says leaving the inflow is not shown to be recovery.

places.states: General laws for any balanced Flow over a Web, with a family ds and conditions beyond it, rest. Where the whole gains nothing, the beyond falls by the family's rise plus what is lost. A rise above the slack of the met dependences beyond breaks one of them, and the dependent formation then ends or its dependence weakens. Every selection rewarding such a rise holds only where an unseen dependence breaks. The share reaching beyond is never selected against and does not fall under transmission. Each law also has a version graded by the inflow. Dweller, WithinSlack, Spreading and Lapsing are built witnesses on the Diversion model.
places.moves: N: there is no Process with a choice among steps. `select : (Nat → C → Nat) → Prop` in favours_breaking_beyond (l. 293) is a predicate on levels, quantified as every selection, not a choice of moves.
places.reading: S: `favours_breaking_beyond` (l. 293). Suppose every condition a member couples into (W.CoupledInto obs) is in ds, rest is apart from ds, rest is met (MetOn), the whole is gainless, and the selection holds only where the family rises above the slack. Then the selection holds only where a formation outside the group has a broken dependence on a condition no member couples into. What members register (their coupling) fixes what the selection cannot see. Flow.reach (l. 355) reads whether a formation takes from beyond, and share_not_against takes `reading : G.amount t p = L.reach rest t p`. B: `Dweller.selected_breaks` (l. 530).
places.share: S: `share_not_against` (l. 394): if the whole is gainless, members are present, and more offspring go only to raisers of ds, then G.discordAt t = 0, so the offspring-weighted share reaching beyond is at least its uniform share. `share_not_lower` (l. 425): under those premises plus transmission, size T · sum 0 ≤ size 0 · sum T. `share_moved_rises` (l. 441): with exact transmission, a share that moved rose, with some step concordant. The offspring rule is a premise (rewarded); it is not set again from the share. B: `Spreading.share_rises` (l. 649), `Lapsing.share_falls` (l. 692).
places.level: S: `Balances.beyond_falls_exactly` (l. 142): if gainless, stock ds (t+1) + stock rest (t+1) + lost = stock ds t + stock rest t. `breaks_beyond` (l. 205): with MetOn and stock ds t + slack < stock ds (t+1) + lost, some condition in rest falls below the need at t (Broken). Web.slack (l. 91) is what the levels stand above the needs. No statement has a return that depends on what is left.
places.giving: S in part: `Balances.breaks_beyond_ends` (l. 256): if W.Dependent holds and the dependence is unchanged at t+1, the formation dep c, whose dependence broke, is not active at t+1. That formation is a going-on of the model that is lost, but it is the one that depends on the level, not the one that gives to it. What gives (L.give) is part of the flow handed in. N for a giver that can be lost.
places.cost: N: no statement has keeping or giving cost the one who does it. `RaisesOn.reaches` (l. 382) concludes that a raiser takes from beyond, which is a draw on the beyond, not on itself.
places.multiplying: S: the share laws (l. 394, l. 425, l. 441) are over SelectionTerm.Generations, whose kids and offspringNumber are units leaving units. That offspring relation is handed in; it is not a law of the flow's step. The account says it need not be descent. B: `Spreading.generations` (l. 617): the taker leaves two takers and the dweller none.
places.no_return: N: no irreversibility is stated. `breaks_beyond_ends` (l. 256) concludes non-activity at the next step only, under premises; nothing says the formation is never active again.
places.both_outcomes: B only: `WithinSlack.within_slack` (l. 568), a rise exactly equal to the slack with the dependence kept, against `Dweller.rise_ends_dweller` (l. 516), the slack exceeded and the dweller ending. Also `Spreading.share_rises` (l. 649) against `Lapsing.share_falls` (l. 692), the same selection with different transmission. There is no general exactly-when; breaks_beyond is one direction.
places.comparison: N for a general law carrying something between two processes or starts. `breaks_beyond_past_free` (l. 216) extends the bound to conditions with no dependence. B: Spreading and Lapsing compare one selection under two transmissions.
places.rank: N: no bound on ending and no falling rank. `Balances.rise_bounded_by_beyond` (l. 331): over a stretch in which every step is gainless, stock ds (S+N) + stock rest (S+N) ≤ stock ds S + stock rest S. `stock_not_rises_over` (l. 310): a family's stock does not rise. These bound the rise; they are not a deadline. `open_of_rise_above` (l. 341): a rise above everything held needs some step that is not gainless.
places.closed_region: N for a general invariant region. B: `Spreading.store_bounded` (l. 672): the store is at most 2 at every step.
places.forms_change: S in part: `Balances.breaks_beyond_unsettles` (l. 244): the formation whose dependence breaks is not, at t+1, active with that dependence at a need at least as strong. It ends, or its dependence weakens or dissolves. No statement has the going on continuing while forms change, or widening.

places.states: It reads DrawnShaping's drawn rule as the weights of Drift.Replacement's one-at-a-time chain among M + 1 members: up (the shapers' count of the rule read), down (the others', constant), and stay. It states that favouring at a count is down ≤ up (favours_iff), that fixation is bounded both ways by the potential (fixation), that either noiseless lock is left with positive weight (lost_ge, fixed_ge), with bounds that fall across the distance to the critical mass (lost_above, fixed_below). It also states the end steps of the potential (one_each) and risk dominance at an even population (risk_dominant_iff). These are general over the parameters a, p, c, hi, lo and M of this one model family; Strong and Weak are built witnesses.
places.moves: N: there are no moves, policy or allowed set. valueBy totals weighted histories of the chain; no step is chosen.
places.reading: S: `favours_iff` (l. 136): at a mixed count i, CarrierCounts.favours (DrawnShaping.drawn … (at_ M i mixed)) ↔ down ≤ up. `drawn_carrier` (l. 124) and `drawn_other` (l. 129): the rule read by readers drawn from the population, shapers reading hi and others lo, is exactly up and down. So what the readers register decides the chain's weights.
places.share: S: the shapers' weight up M a p hi lo i (l. 101) is read from the count i, so the chain's step weights are set again from the count. `up_mono` (l. 144): with lo ≤ hi, up does not fall as i grows, so favouring at a count holds at every higher count.
places.level: N: there is no stock or reserve that runs down.
places.giving: N: no statement has something that gives to a level, or keeps a condition met.
places.cost: D/S: the account (from DrawnShaping) calls c the cost of shaping. In the statements, c enters only through the others' weight, down = (M+1)(a + c + p) (l. 104). `risk_dominant_iff` (l. 259): at an even population the shapers are favoured strictly iff 2c < hi + lo. No statement has a cost to the one who shapes as an act spent.
places.multiplying: S: the chain draws a member to leave offspring and replace one of the other kind, with weights up i and down i (account; `steps` l. 158: up + down + stay = whole at every mixed count). The count changes by these step weights. `fixation` (l. 196) applies Drift.Replacement.fixationBy.
places.no_return: S: either noiseless lock is left, with positive weight. `lost_ge` (l. 211): from i ≤ M, the histories losing every shaper weigh at least ((M+1)(a+c+p))^i · whole^k. `fixed_ge` (l. 217): from 0 < i with M + 1 ≤ i + k, fixing weighs at least a^k. The absorbing ends, fixed and lost, are absorbing by the chain's definition in Drift (valueBy_stays), not concluded here.
places.both_outcomes: S: `fixation` (l. 196) bounds the histories fixing the shapers on both sides by the potential; the remainder is lost or varied, the varied vanishing geometrically. These are weights over histories, not an exactly-when for one course. `favours_iff` and `risk_dominant_iff` are iffs about favouring. B: `Strong.other_first` (l. 277): risk dominant, yet one other fixes with more weight. `Weak.shapers_first` (l. 289) and `Weak.shared_decides` (l. 295): the reverse.
places.comparison: S: `drawn_carrier` / `drawn_other` (l. 124, l. 129) carry DrawnShaping's counts into the chain's weights as equalities. `lost_above` (l. 225) and `fixed_below` (l. 239) bound losing above the mass and fixing below it by products of the weights across a stretch. B: Strong against Weak, the same c, hi and lo with a different a or p.
places.rank: S: `fixation` (l. 196), with r + a^(M+1) = whole^(M+1): the histories still varied after m rounds of M + 1 steps weigh at most r^m, a geometric bound inherited from Drift.Replacement.fixationBy. `lost_above` (l. 225) bounds the weight of losing by t · down^n · whole^k over the shapers' weights. These are weight bounds, not a falling variant.
places.closed_region: N: no closed region is stated in this module. The ends fixed and lost stay by Drift.Replacement.valueBy's definition. The noiseless locks of DrawnShaping are shown not to be closed under drift (lost_ge, fixed_ge).
places.forms_change: S in part: `lost_ge` (l. 211) and `fixed_ge` (l. 217): from every mixed count both locks are left with positive weight, so the kind present can change until one fixes. No statement has a going on that continues with kinds coming and going, or widens.
