places.place: RuleRebuilding.lean: step, net, Ends, Gone, Held, NoHolder, Band, Within, «恒取不逾生则存», «恒取逾生则尽», «稳者恒持当且仅当在带», «稳开二试», «域闭», «不及任则持尽», «无持者不复», «无持者改不行», «尽而不复», «无持而门开众在», «域中任满皆新», «隙之律», «同规随类»
places.states: One family of nets, built: a Rule with parameters tenure, teaching age, renewal, untaught, strength and source. A state St holds a quota, a level, and holder and other counts by cohort. One step draws the take (all members), renews by g, enters holders taught from teachers and others past a door that reads the teachers, ages the cohorts and revises the quota. The laws are stated for every parameter value under hypotheses: the constant-take lemma, the band iff for the steady state («稳者恒持当且仅当在带»), a closed region with free revision («域闭»), drains («不及任则持尽», «额零则持尽»), no holder from no holder («无持者不复»), the end closed («尽而不复»), open entry, two tests compared («稳开二试»), and the gaps law («隙之律»). Witnesses are given at particular rules (rA to rI).
places.moves: S: `Move` (l. 152) is a choice at each step: whether entrants are on offer, and an optional revision. `net r x y := ∃ m, y = step r m x` (l. 226) is 'the net of the possible'. Laws over every choice: `«尽而不复»` (l. 457) says Gone is closed under the whole net. `«无持者不复»` (l. 698) says NoHolder is closed under the whole net for source members or none. `«不及任则持尽»` (l. 658) drains for every course c. `«域闭»` (l. 1197) says Within P Q is closed under every step with entrants on offer and a revision in [P, Q].
places.reading: S: the door and the entry read only the teachers' count: `teachers` (l. 177), `taught` (l. 180), `door` (l. 194). `«无持者额不与»` (l. 773): two no-holder states differing only in quota have the same later level and members along every course, so the quota is read by nothing. `«同规随类»` (l. 1896): at rB, a step with a revision inside the region continues (`«续»` on net rB) under the class 'held or not' and not under the class 'same quota'. Whether it continues is decided by the class read.
places.share: S, partly: no fraction. The teachers' count T sets both the new holders (the quota if T > 0, else 0, under source members: `taught` l. 180) and the others admitted (f − c·T, truncated: `door` l. 194). So entry is set again at each step from the count of holders old enough to teach. The `leak` (l. 246) is f − c·q·(s−l) at a quota.
places.level: S: the level is drawn by `take` (l. 174, the sum of members) and renewed by a constant g. A step `Ends` (l. 214) where the level is 0 or level + g < take. `«恒取不逾生则存»` (l. 493): with a constant take A ≤ g, in a family closed under non-ending steps, from level ≥ 1, the level does not fall. `«恒取逾生则减»` (l. 509): with take g+d, the level falls by d a step. `«恒取逾生则尽»` (l. 539): it is Gone at some step k+1. What comes back is the constant g while anything is left, and nothing once Gone (`«尽而不复»`).
places.giving: S, for what keeps Held met: the holders who teach are themselves counts of the model that drain. `«不及任则持尽»` (l. 658): with s ≤ l, no holder is left after s steps. `«无持者不复»` (l. 698): with no holder, no holder ever again under source members or none. `«三源之表»` (l. 1519): from an empty membership, taught from outside the rule is held after one step, otherwise not. N, for the level: the renewal g is a constant parameter of Rule, not a going-on.
places.cost: N: no statement of a cost to the keeper beyond its own draw. `take` (l. 174) counts holders and others alike. D: the account (l. 36-37) says both draw alike, a keeper draws on what it keeps, and nothing is a cost of keeping beyond that. S, related: `«稳存而开不存则门过一»` (l. 1390): where the steady state takes within g and open entry does not, 2 ≤ c·(s−l), i.e. a keeper turns away more than itself.
places.multiplying: S: holders leave holders. Under source members, a new cohort of q holders enters exactly when the teachers' count is positive (`taught` l. 180, `entrant` l. 187, `onward_steady` l. 809). `onward_strands` (l. 1702): at l = s−1 each cohort teaches exactly the one that replaces it, and held cohorts only rotate. The number entering is fixed by the quota, not by the number of teachers.
places.no_return: S: `«尽而不复»` (l. 457): Gone is closed under the net. This is a premise built into the step (Ends sends to ⟨q,0,[],[]⟩), as the account says (l. 71). `«无持者不复»` (l. 698), concluded from the step: with no holder, no holder at every later step under source members or none. `«无持者改不行»` (l. 737): a revision without a holder does not change the quota. `«改额为零则持尽»` (l. 1457): a revision to 0 with no later nonzero revision leaves no holder s steps on. These are at the loss of the teachers, who are what keeps the rule held. B: `«及任之前持尽之例»` (l. 1955).
places.both_outcomes: S: `«稳者恒持当且仅当在带»` (l. 897): source members, always on, no revision, level ≥ 1. From steady q L the rule is held at every step ↔ Band (l < s, 1 ≤ q, (q + leak q)·s ≤ g), and otherwise `steady_ends` (l. 872) reaches Gone. `«外授之稳同带»` (l. 922) is the same from outside. `«稳开二试»` (l. 1368): Goes ↔ the take test, and otherwise EndsUp, for the steady state and for `nobody`. `«存尽相斥»` (l. 1351): they exclude each other. `«隙之律»` (l. 1772): held at every step ↔ k·(q+e) + z·f ≤ g; and `«隙过生持至尽»` (l. 1792): over it, held to the last state before Gone. All of this built family, general over parameters.
places.comparison: S: `«稳开二试»` (l. 1368) compares two separately started states, each with its own test. `«四境皆有»` (l. 1942): all four combinations occur. `«无持者额不与»` (l. 773): two starts differing only in quota run alike in level, holders and others. `«三源之表»` (l. 1519) compares the three sources. `«隙存而稳不存之式»` (l. 1827) and `«稳存而隙不存之式»` (l. 1841) are the arithmetic of where one holds and the other does not. N: no simulation, and no order kept by the step between two courses.
places.rank: S: `«恒取逾生则减»` (l. 509): the level falls by d each step from r₀ + k·d. `«恒取逾生则尽»` (l. 539): Gone at step k+1. `drain_of` (l. 634): where no holder enters, holders are 0 after tenure s steps, a deadline. `«不及任则持尽»` (l. 658), `«额零则持尽»` (l. 677) and `«无持而门开逾生则尽»` (l. 1292): with no holder and g < f·s, Gone at some step.
places.closed_region: S: `«域闭»` (l. 1197): Within P Q is closed under onIn (on, revision in [P, Q]) given Fits r P Q. `«域中储不减»` (l. 1203): the level does not fall in it. `«稳为域之例»` (l. 1216): the steady state is a case of it. `«尽而不复»` (l. 457) and `«无持者不复»` (l. 698): closed under the whole net. `Closed` (l. 487), `steady_closed` (l. 841) and `strands_closed` (l. 1740) are families closed under non-ending steps. B: `«域可得»` (l. 1225) at rB, 3 to 5.
places.forms_change: S: `«域中任满皆新»` (l. 1582): in the region, with revisions in [P, Q], after s steps the rule is held and still in the region, and its holders are exactly the cohorts entered in those steps, each at the quota then standing (`«任满皆新»` l. 1546). `«无持而门开众在»` (l. 1276) and `«无持而门开不逾生则存»` (l. 1255): after the rule is lost, others are present after every step and the level does not fall, where f·s ≤ g. B: `«同规随类»` (l. 1896): it continues under 'held or not' while the quota changes. `«改而成隙则尽»` (l. 1885): revision to 0 and back makes gaps, then ends. `«弃而储增»` (l. 1921): no member and the level risen. N: no widening.

places.giving: S: the givers to offspring standing are formations present in the flow, typically the parents, and the bounds charge offspring to the parent's own prior standing (`parent_within_inflow` l. 274, `parent_within_factor` l. 696). Which formations are present is supplied by the Flow, and no general law here states the loss of a giver. B: in `Displacement` (defs `level` l. 973, `takeFirst` l. 994) the carrier, the other member and the pool stand at 0 after the first step. In `Inherited` and `Fed` (by docstrings) the offspring become the givers at the next step.
places.cost: S: `parent_within_inflow` (l. 274) and `parent_within_factor` (l. 696): beyond the inflow, a parent's offspring are bounded by its own standing before the step, capped at m. B: `Displacement.takeFirst` (l. 994): the carrier takes one unit from itself and stands at 0 after. Docstrings in `Fed` (l. 1332) and `Uncapped` (l. 2248) say the parent or carrier takes its units from itself.
places.multiplying: S: in Generations, units leave units (the family at t+1 is the offspring of the family at t). `generation_within_inflow` (l. 291): m × next size ≤ standing + inflow. `total_within_factor` (l. 715): next total ≤ k × this total under a per-parent inflow cap. `total_within_power` (l. 733): ≤ k^T over T steps. B: `Fed.fed` (l. 1574) sizes 2, 2, 4; `Inherited.stretch_attained` (l. 2071) total 1 to 4.
places.no_return: N: no point of no return or irreversibility is stated in the module. D: the account cites `Reproduction.Flow.closed_lineage_lowered` (closed lineage ended) from another module, not stated here.
places.both_outcomes: N: no exactly-when or dichotomy of going on versus ending, or of keeping versus losing. The witnesses contrast laws holding (`Displacement.displacement` l. 1130) with candidate laws failing (`Displacement.natural_fails` l. 1146, `Inherited.same_step_fails` l. 2009, `Uncapped.uncapped`, `Shrink.shrink` l. 2505), but these are counterexamples to bounds.
places.comparison: N: no law carries something between two processes, starts or ways. Nearest: `inflow_lineage_le` (l. 501) and `joint_within_carried` (l. 553) compare inflow into a joint lineage with the sum over single lineages; `Displacement.least` (l. 1210) and `Fed.least` (l. 1605) state, for any world meeting the premises with given counts, a least inflow.
places.rank: S, as lower bounds on time, not ending: `steps_to_move` (l. 673): m × the mean's cross-multiplied move over T steps ≤ first size × T·I where each step carries at most I. `whole_within_power` (l. 781): reaching the whole needs first size ≤ k^T × first total (T ≥ log_k(N/c)). N: no variant that falls to an end, drain or deadline of ending.
places.closed_region: N: no law of a region closed under steps. B: `Displacement.closed` (l. 1056) and `Inherited.closedFirst`/`closedSecond` (l. 1872): the built family is closed at the step (a premise of the witness, used to show the inflow is nothing).
places.forms_change: B: `Displacement.displacement` (l. 1130): the population's size stays at two while its members change (carrier and other replaced by two offspring) and the carriers' share goes from half to whole. `Inherited.stretch_attained` (l. 2071): over two steps the generations relay and the total goes from 1 to 4. S (structure only): `standing_pinned` (l. 308): members of the next generation, capped at m and standing at m or more, stand at exactly m; generations are supplied as each the offspring of the last.

places.states: For any web and group, some selection through the pooled coupling separates two histories exactly when not every member couples them alike (`Web.separates_all_iff`), or, with the members listed and decided, exactly when some member does (`Web.separates_all_iff_member`). Under an act that differs only beyond the pool's coupling closure, with the rest following a law reading through coupling, every pooled selection of a group within the closure selects the two flows alike, and only formations beyond the closure couple them apart (`Flow.act_unselected_pool`, `Flow.apart_beyond_pool`, `Flow.act_selected_by_pool`). Reading another's couplings reaches no further than pooling with it (`Flow.unselected_beyond_reads`, `Flow.act_unselected_reads`), and a majority reading selects through the pooled coupling and can outvote a minority's distinction (`Web.majority_through_all`, `Web.majority_outvoted`). These laws are general; `Clearing` is the built witness.

Then every selection through the pooled coupling of any group within the closure selects the two courses' levels alike. So every choice of act that differs only beyond the closure keeps the pooled selection the same.

So every selection that holds only where the family a group couples into rises holds only where some formation takes from a condition no member couples into (`Flow.favours_reaching_beyond(_inflow)`). places.place: SelectionShift.lean: Generations.shift_step, Generations.never_empties_of_unbounded, Generations.goes_on_iff, Generations.goes_on, Horizon.same_terms_two_fates, Horizon.eventually_zero_two_fates, Horizon.terms_boundary, Generations.nonempty_before, Shrinking.positive_then_empty
places.states: For every course of generations (`SelectionTerm.Generations`: a first family, given offspring lists per step, given amounts), the selection term proper (concordance and discordance of offspring number with amount) is unchanged by a common shift of offspring numbers while the next generation's size moves (`Generations.shift_step`), a positive term at a step makes the next generation nonempty, a term positive at unboundedly many steps makes every generation nonempty, and read by offspring number with exact transmission from t on, every later generation is nonempty exactly where generation t+1 is (`goes_on_iff`). Also general, by constructions from any G: within any horizon H two courses share G's terms through H and have the same terms everywhere, one going on and one ending (`Horizon.same_terms_two_fates`), and for terms zero after some step a course that goes on and one that ends share all of G's terms (`eventually_zero_two_fates`, joined in `terms_boundary`); built witnesses (OneLine, ExactOnce, ZeroTerm, steady, Alternating, Shrinking) show premises hold together or cannot be narrowed.
places.moves: N: no process with a choice among steps, policy or allowed set; each `Generations` has one given offspring function `kids t` per step. The `Horizon` constructions (`keep` l. 578, `going` l. 585, `ending` l. 589, `goingShifted` l. 765) build alternative courses from G, but no law is about what some or every choice keeps.
places.reading: S: `SameTerms` (l. 570) and `Horizon.same_terms_two_fates` (l. 664): for every G and H, `going G H` and `ending G H` have G's families through H+1 and G's concordance and discordance through H, the same terms as each other at every step, and the first is as large as G at H+1 from H+1 on while the second is empty from H+2 on; so what the selection term registers does not decide the fate within a horizon. S: `Horizon.terms_boundary` (l. 941): for G nonempty at its first generation, terms positive at unboundedly many steps are shared only by courses nonempty at every generation; terms zero after some H are shared by a course nonempty everywhere and one empty from some generation on. S: `Generations.goes_on` (l. 381): read by offspring number (`Reproduction.Generations.ByNumber`) with exact transmission from t on, positive concordance at t forces every later generation nonempty.
places.share: N: concordance and discordance are counts over ordered pairs, not a share of one kind among several, and no rule or favouring is set again from them; the offspring function is given per step. (B: `Shrinking.positive_then_empty` l. 1123 states a mark total of one at every step through N, not a share driving the step.)
places.level: S: the only amount that runs down is the family size: `Generations.nonempty_before` (l. 327): a generation nonempty at s means every earlier one is nonempty (an empty family stays empty), and `shift_step` (l. 263) gives size (t+1) = G.size (t+1) + G.size t * k for the shifted course, so the next size depends on the present members. No stock or reserve with a return depending on what is left. B: `Shrinking.positive_then_empty` (l. 1123): the family shrinks by one at each step and is empty from N+1 on.
places.giving: S: what gives the next generation is the members themselves, units of the model that can be lost: `Generations.next_of_reproducing` (l. 292): a member of the family at t with a positive offspring number makes generation t+1 nonempty; `Generations.line_kept` (l. 346): read by offspring number with exact transmission from t on, a member with positive offspring number keeps a line carrying that offspring number in every later generation. But each member's offspring list is handed in (`kids`), not derived.
places.cost: N: no statement in which keeping or giving costs the member that does it.
places.multiplying: S: members leave members: the family at t+1 is the offspring of the family at t (definition in SelectionTerm), and `Generations.shift_step` (l. 263) states the next size moves by k for each member when offspring numbers shift by k; `next_of_selection` (l. 298) a positive term makes the next generation nonempty. The number changes by the given offspring numbers, not by a law of the step from a state.
places.no_return: S, concluded: `Generations.nonempty_before` (l. 327): an empty family stays empty (from `Reproduction.Generations.empty_from`); this is at the loss of every member, i.e. of all that gives. S: `Generations.last_term_zero` (l. 305): where the next generation is empty, both terms are zero at the step. No statement of a point from which no course keeps it. B: `ExactOnce.exact_once_ends` (l. 509), `Horizon.ending_empty` (l. 648), `Shrinking.positive_then_empty` (l. 1123).
places.both_outcomes: S, general: `Generations.goes_on_iff` (l. 364): with `ByNumber G` and exact transmission at every step from t, every later generation is nonempty iff generation t+1 is. S, general construction: `Horizon.same_terms_two_fates` (l. 664), `two_fates_of_nonempty` (l. 811), `zero_after_two_fates` (l. 873), `eventually_zero_two_fates` (l. 911): one course of terms shared by a going and an ending course. `terms_boundary` (l. 941) states two cases, not a decision between them. B: `Shrinking.positive_then_empty` (l. 1123): positive concordance at every step before N, then empty.
places.comparison: S: `Generations.shift_step` (l. 263): two courses G, G' alike at t in family and amounts, offspring numbers of G' those of G plus k, have equal concordance and discordance at t and G'.size (t+1) = G.size (t+1) + G.size t * k. S: `Horizon.terms_boundary` (l. 941) first part: for every G' with `SameTerms G G'`, where G's terms are positive at unboundedly many steps, G' is nonempty at every generation (carried between courses sharing terms). S: `Horizon.same_terms_two_fates` (l. 664) and `keep_family`/`keep_terms` (l. 601, 612) carry families and terms from G to the constructed courses through H.
places.rank: B: `Shrinking.positive_then_empty` (l. 1123): for every N, a built course whose family shrinks by one each step is empty from N+1 on (an end within N+1 steps). S only as a proof device: `Horizon.eventually_zero_two_fates` (l. 911) recurses down on H to the last nonempty generation. No general law of a falling rank or variant.
places.closed_region: S: `Generations.line_kept` (l. 346): with `ByNumber G` and exact transmission from t, for a member p at t with positive offspring number, at every n some member of generation t+n has p's offspring number (an invariant carried along). S: `Horizon.going_family` (l. 637): from H+1 on, `going G H`'s family equals G's family at H+1 (a fixed family). B: `Horizon.steady_family` (l. 721), `Alternating.course_family` (l. 980): the family is [true, false] at every step.
places.forms_change: N: no statement in which the going on continues while what is present changes; in the constructions each member leaves itself after H (`going`), and `OneLine`, `steady`, `Alternating` keep the same family. D: the opening account (modelling choices, l. 118-125) says a line whose descendants change kind, or a revival, is not distinguished here, and newness is not represented. B: in `Shrinking` (l. 1050-1123) the members change label (some m to some (m-1)) but the course ends.
places.how_read: All statements read, the whole module (l. 1-1149); states, reading, level, giving, multiplying, no_return, both_outcomes, comparison, closed_region answered from statements, rank and forms_change from built cases (forms_change also from the account), moves, share and cost N.

places.states: General: for every finite list with natural-number weights and amounts, the number of members times the weighted total plus discordance equals total weight times total amount plus concordance (`covariation`), so the weighted total exceeds its uniform share exactly where concordance exceeds discordance (`selection_exceeds_iff`), and with transmission Price's equation in counting form (`offspring_covariation`). Over every course of `Generations` the mean amount moves by the selection term and transmission together (`mean_step`), kept or rising exactly where balanced or raising, a moved mean has an unbalanced step (by selection with exact transmission, by transmission with uniform offspring numbers), and on flows where only active formations give and activity needs support a reading highest at supported members is never selected against and its mean does not fall (`Flow.support_not_against`, `support_not_lower`, `support_moved_rises`); built witnesses `Rising`, `Doubling`, `SupportedDescent`.

S: `Generations.moved_by_selection` (l. 608): with exact transmission over a stretch, a moved mean has a step where discordance differs from concordance; `selection_exceeds_iff` (l. 327).
places.share: S: the uniform share (born · total over the number of parents) and the mean (sum over size, compared by cross-multiplying): `selection_exceeds_iff` (l. 327), `selection_none_iff` (l. 332), `share_le_of_below` (l. 374), `kept_step_iff` (l. 483). N: no rule or favouring set again from a share; the offspring lists are given.

Support enters only as the premise `W.Supported t p` (defined in Dependence) through `support_not_against` (l. 389). Family size reaches zero only as `empty_after` (l. 493).
places.giving: S, as premises handed in: `Flow.support_not_against` (l. 389) and `support_not_lower` (l. 648) take `L.Acting W` (only active formations give) and `W.Dependent` (activity needs support), so an unsupported parent leaves no offspring (via `Flow.unsupported_childless` of Evolution); the givers are formations of the flow, but their being supported is a premise, not a going-on derived here.
places.cost: N: no statement in which giving or keeping costs the giver.
places.multiplying: S: `Generations.family` (l. 421): the family at t+1 is the offspring of the family at t; `Generations.born_eq` (l. 448): the number of offspring is the next generation's size; offspring lists given per step.

places.place: SetPointOptimum.lean: Optimum.Nearing, Optimum.atSetPoint_of_reach, Optimum.atSetPoint_iff, Flow.Balances.atSetPoint_draws, Flow.Balances.atSetPoint_broken_iff, Optimum.nearing_beyond, Flow.held_excess_ends, HeldPair.held_end
places.states: S: General laws, stated for every family, set point, order and balanced flow, about orders nearing a set point (`Optimum.Nearing`, l. 196). Where some eligible outcome stands at the set point, every optimum stands there (`atSetPoint_of_reach`, l. 315; exactly, `atSetPoint_iff`, l. 300). Below the set point a nearing order rises and its optima take the part's whole capacity beyond (`nearing_beyond`, l. 669). In a balanced step where the whole gains nothing, reaching the set point draws a fixed total from beyond and breaks a dependence past the slack (`Flow.Balances.atSetPoint_draws`, l. 526; `atSetPoint_breaks`, l. 549). Formations that hold their levels and lose together more than a condition is given end every formation that depends on it (`Flow.held_excess_ends`, l. 759). Built witnesses: Drain, Topped, Spread, Skew, TwoStores, HeldPair.
places.moves: S: The choice is an optimum (`Frontier eligible better o`) among eligible outcomes, or among the outcomes `Flow.Outcome` opens to a part in an exchange. It is not a `Process S A`. `atSetPoint_of_reach` (l. 315): every optimum of every nearing order stands at the set point wherever some eligible outcome does. `optima_iff` (l. 340): an outcome is an optimum of some nearing order exactly where it is eligible and at the set point. `nearing_beyond` (l. 669): every nearing optimum standing below its set point at a condition of the family stands beyond at the level before plus what the rest gives, less what the rest takes, less the part's whole capacity. D: the opening account says the course of choices is not formalized (l. 92-93).
places.reading: S: A nearing order reads only the family `ds`; `byGap` (l. 209) ranks by the family's total gap, and an outcome at the set point is beaten by none whatever it holds beyond (`byGap_unbeaten_at`, l. 256). `least_at_iff` (l. 353): every optimum of every nearing order stands at the least level beyond exactly where all eligible outcomes at the set point stand alike beyond, so the class leaves the beyond undecided. `Flow.held_excess_ends` (l. 759) concludes `¬ W.CoupledInto obs h c` for every holder whose couplings lie in its family apart from `c`: those that end the condition do not couple into it. B: `HeldPair.held_end` (l. 1513): the renewal ends and neither holder couples into the pool. `Topped.counted_after_keeps` (l. 991): a term on the beyond counted after the set point keeps the need.
places.share: N: no count or fraction of one kind among several, and no rule set again from one, in any statement read.
places.level: S: Levels and stocks (`W.level`, `W.stock`) with needs and slack. `Flow.Balances.atSetPoint_breaks` (l. 549): where the set point's total plus what the whole loses exceeds the family before plus the slack, some dependence beyond is broken. `Flow.held_excess_ends` (l. 759) has premises `gated` (each present formation that gives to `c` requires `c` at a need of at least `m`), `dependent`, `start : W.level T c < n + m` and joint losses exceeding what outsiders give at each step. From these it concludes every formation depending on `c` at a need of at least `m` is inactive from `T + n` on. So what gives back depends on the level left.
places.giving: S: In `Flow.held_excess_ends` (l. 759), what gives to `c` is a formation of the model (premises `gated` and `W.Dependent`), and the conclusion is that every such dependent formation is inactive from `T + n` on. The giver is lost, not a function handed in. B: `HeldPair.held_end` (l. 1513): the renewer, the only giver to the pool (`gated`, l. 1402), depends on the pool at need one and is inactive after two steps.
places.cost: N: no statement read has the keeping or giving cost the one who does it. `Flow.held_draws` (l. 729) states the reverse: a formation holding its family's stock and losing `l` (premise `loses`) takes from the condition `c` at least what it gives there plus `l`, so the cost is drawn from `c`.
places.multiplying: N: no units leave units and no kinds form kinds; the formations are fixed lists (`present`).
places.no_return: S: `Flow.held_excess_ends` (l. 759) concludes `∀ k g, W.requires (T+n+k) g c → m ≤ W.need (T+n+k) g c → ¬ W.active (T+n+k) g`: inactive at every step from `T + n` on. This is concluded from premises over `n` steps (via `Flow.joint_excess_ends`, in another module) and is at the loss of what gives (the gated givers). `atSetPoint_breaks` / `atSetPoint_broken_iff` conclude a break at one step only, not that it stays broken. B: `HeldPair.held_end` (l. 1513).
places.both_outcomes: S: `Flow.Balances.atSetPoint_broken_iff` (l. 562): with one condition beyond depended on at a need it meets, across a balanced gainless step to the set point the dependence is broken exactly where `W.stock ds t + (level - need) < total ds s + lost`. This is general, of one step. `atSetPoint_iff` (l. 300) and `counted_after_keeps_iff` (l. 409) are further exactly-when statements, general, about optima. B: `Drain.kept_iff` (l. 836): the dweller's need is met exactly where `k ≤ 1`. `Topped.nearing_either` (l. 966): the order by distance has both a keeping optimum and a draining one.
places.comparison: S: `Optimum.nearing_as_rising` (l. 682): below its set point, a nearing optimum stands at each condition beyond where every optimum of every rising order stands. `Nearing.mono` (l. 236): every order ranking above wherever a nearing order does is nearing, a class closed upward. `mutual_atSetPoint` (l. 326) and `Flow.Balances.mutual_atSetPoint_draws` (l. 598): several optimizers draw what one optimizer with their joint set point draws.
places.rank: S: `Flow.held_excess_ends` (l. 759) is a deadline: where the level of `c` at `T` is below `n + m` and joint losses exceed what is given at each of `n` steps, the dependents are inactive from `T + n` on. No falling variant is stated in this module; the bound comes from `Flow.joint_excess_ends`.
places.closed_region: N: no region closed under steps, invariant or largest closed set is stated. `Optimum.stock_eq_of_atSetPoint` (l. 715) states only that a family at its set point at two steps has equal stock at them. D: the account (l. 91-93) says a nearing chooser holds its family at the set point wherever an eligible outcome reaches it at each step, and that the course of choices is not formalized.
places.forms_change: N: no statement or built case read has the going on continue while what is present changes, and none has more go on after. HeldPair reuses the members of `Witnesses.relay` (l. 1267) but states no relay.
places.how_read: Every declaration's statement and docstring read, l. 1-1528, with most proof bodies of the witnesses. All answers are from statements except closed_region, which is N with a D note; nothing is U.

places.place: Settling.lean: Settling.ChangeRecurs, Settling.keeps_changing_iff, Settling.settles_no_undoable, Settling.recurs_of_undoable, Settling.loop_of_recurs, Settling.OneWay.lpo_of_settles
places.states: S: General, for every `Process S A`: a run whose change recurs does not settle (`not_settles_of_recurs`, l. 62). In a world a list holds, some run from `s` keeps changing exactly where a configuration reachable from `s` has a step to another configuration from which it can be reached again (`keeps_changing_iff`, l. 302; `keeps_changing_iff_loop`, l. 293). Where every run settles, no reachable step can be undone (`settles_no_undoable`, l. 313). B: in the two-configuration `OneWay`, no run keeps changing (`never_keeps_changing`, l. 369), yet every run from `false` settling gives LPO (`lpo_of_settles`, l. 377).
places.moves: S: `Process S A` with runs (`Run P`). `keeps_changing_iff` (l. 302): some run (some choice of steps) from `s` keeps changing exactly where a reachable undoable step exists. `settles_no_undoable` (l. 313) and `assured_no_undoable` (l. 322): where every run from `s` settles, or rests with its target met, no reachable step to another configuration can be undone.
places.reading: N: no reading, observation or registered class in any statement read.
places.share: N: no shares in any statement read.
places.level: N: no level or amount in any statement read.
places.giving: N: nothing gives to anything in any statement read.
places.cost: N: no cost in any statement read.
places.multiplying: N: no units or kinds that multiply.
places.no_return: S: `settles_no_undoable` (l. 313): where every run from `s` settles, no configuration reachable from `s` has a step to another configuration from which it can be reached again. Irreversibility is concluded from settling, and it concerns configurations, not a level or a giver. B: `OneWay.no_undoable` (l. 359): from `true` every step stays at `true`, so `false` cannot be reached again.
places.both_outcomes: S: `keeps_changing_iff` (l. 302): in a world a list holds, keeping changing on some run holds exactly where some reachable change can be undone. This is general and of one process, but it is a dichotomy of keeping changing against not, not of going on against ending. B: `OneWay.lpo_of_settles` (l. 377) shows that no run keeping changing does not constructively give settling.
places.comparison: N: no law carries anything between two processes or two starts. `recurs_of_loop` (l. 157) builds a second run of the same process from the same configuration.
places.rank: N: no bound on settling, falling variant or deadline. The `OneWay` statements show that no step of settling can be given without LPO.
places.closed_region: N: no invariant or closed region is stated here. `Enough.Settles` and `Enough.Rests` come from `Becoming.Enough`; `Invariant.reach` is used only inside the proof of `OneWay.no_undoable`.
places.forms_change: S: `recurs_of_undoable` (l. 262), through `round` (l. 121) and `round_recurs` (l. 135): a reachable step that can be undone gives a run that goes round the loop again and again, its configuration changing at arbitrarily late steps (`ChangeRecurs`, l. 54). This is an alternation of one process's configurations, not of kinds coming and going, and nothing widens.
places.how_read: The whole module read, l. 1-402, statements, docstrings and proofs. moves, no_return, both_outcomes and forms_change are answered from statements; the rest are N; nothing is U.

places.place: SharedCodes.lean: SharedCodes.hearBy, run_origin, agrees_every_start_iff, shared_iff_in_use, never_agrees_of_both, all_agree_rest, run_imposed_stays, outside_needed, coined_returns, written_rests, omitted_rest, added_never_replaced, majority
places.states: S: General laws for codes `I → M → F` that change only by hearings under a rule (`hearBy`, l. 201; `process`, l. 459). A hearing makes no form (`hearBy_held`, l. 244; `run_held`, l. 550). The form reached is fixed by the start and the order (`run_origin`, l. 377; `agrees_every_start_iff`, l. 388; `shared_iff_in_use`, l. 450). A law keeping both an exchange of formations and a renaming of forms never brings a symmetric disagreement to agreement (`never_agrees_of_both`, l. 921). An imposed code stays along every run, and a merged distinction comes back only from outside or by coining (`run_imposed_stays`, l. 1069; `outside_needed`, l. 1078; `coined_returns`, l. 1368). A reading written back rests and locks (`written_rests`, l. 1183; `omitted_rest`, l. 1240; `added_never_replaced`, l. 1271). Built: TwoFormations, Path, Majority, Gloss.
places.moves: S: `process adopt : Process (I → M → F) (Hearing I M)` (l. 459); each step is a chosen hearing. Laws about every choice: `run_agreement_kept` (l. 495) keeps agreement along every run whose hearings are closed for the group; `all_agree_rest` (l. 529) holds on every run under every rule; `run_imposed_stays` (l. 1069) holds along every run from an imposition. About some choice: `run_shared_iff_in_use` (l. 637), where a list holds every formation: some run brings all to form `x` at `m` exactly where some formation holds `x` there at the start.
places.reading: S: `TellsApart` (l. 700), `ReadsAs` (l. 704). `reads_iff` (l. 714): a reader whose code tells senses apart reads another's form for `m` as `m`, and only `m`, exactly where their codes agree at `m`; `reads_other` (l. 721): otherwise it reads another sense. Records read by `resolve` (l. 1141) decide what each next generation writes (`nextCohort`, l. 1147). `written_rests` (l. 1183): a resolution written back is the only record from the next generation on. `no_reading_recovers` (l. 1210): every reading of later records reads two histories that resolved alike as one. `omitted_rest` (l. 1240): where the records resolve to `e ≠ t`, `t` is no candidate at any later generation. `renamed_carries_iff` (l. 746): a renamed description carries a law exactly where the description does.
places.share: S: `holders` (l. 1383) counts the formations holding a form at a sense. `majority` (l. 1388) has each formation take a form held by more than half, where there is one. `majority_held` (l. 1394): taking what most hold makes no form. This is one application of the rule; no law of the rule set again over a run. B: `Majority.odd_agrees` (l. 1413): two of three agree at once. `Majority.even_rests` (l. 1420): one of two rests.
places.level: N: no stock or amount that runs down in any statement read.
places.giving: N: no level is given to. What is lost is a distinction (`Loses`, l. 1033), not something a going-on gives.
places.cost: N: no cost to the one who keeps or gives. `impose_loses_iff` (l. 1052) and `source_loses_nothing` (l. 1056) state what imposition takes from the other formations; the source loses nothing.
places.multiplying: N: the formations are fixed; generations are record lists under `Law.run`, not units leaving units.
places.no_return: S, concluded and not at a level. `all_agree_rest` (l. 529): once all formations agree at `m`, no form at `m` changes on any run under any rule. `held_stays` (l. 1063) and `run_imposed_stays` (l. 1069): an imposed code stays at every later step and every merge stays. `outside_needed` (l. 1078): if every formation inside and outside the group holds the imposed form at `m`, every formation holds it at every later step. `resolved_alike_merged` (l. 1202) and `no_reading_recovers` (l. 1210): earlier records are never recovered. `omitted_rest` (l. 1240): the omitted target is never a candidate again. The return needs coining, a step hearing lacks (`coined_returns`, l. 1368).
places.both_outcomes: S (general, of keeping against losing agreement or distinctions). `kept_iff` (l. 303) and `run_kept_iff` (l. 515): a group's agreement is kept by a hearing exactly unless a member hears the sense, the rule takes the form and the speaker's form differs. `keeps_apart_iff` (l. 823): a hearing keeps the hearer's code telling senses apart exactly where the form taken is not one the hearer gives another sense. `agrees_every_start_iff` (l. 388) and `follow_agrees_iff` (l. 674) are further exactly-when statements. No dichotomy of going on against ending.
places.comparison: S: `run_renamed` (l. 980): two runs through one order, from starts differing by a renaming, differ by that renaming at every step. `reached_differ_iff` (l. 995). `keeps_both` (l. 897): a law keeping an exchange and a renaming keeps the two together. `Law.Commutes.keepsRelation` (l. 176): a law commuting with `σ` keeps the relation of a configuration to its image. `run_renamed_tells_apart_iff` (l. 1007) and `renamed_carries_iff` (l. 746).
places.rank: N: no bound, falling variant or deadline. D: the account says the time agreement takes is not derived (l. 146-147).
places.closed_region: S: `agreement_kept` (l. 296) and `run_agreement_kept` (l. 495): a group's agreement is closed under hearings closed for it. `all_agree_rest` (l. 529): agreement of all is a rest. `held_stays` (l. 1063): a form all hold stays under every order and rule. `written_rests` (l. 1183) and `kept_rests` (l. 1294): the resolution written back is a rest of `nextCohort` and of `keep`. `agrees_only_fixed` (l. 905): a symmetric start stays symmetric under a kept symmetry, via `Law.KeepsRelation.run` from `Becoming.IdentificationRuns`.
places.forms_change: S: `coined_returns` (l. 1368): where all hold a code merging `m` and `m'`, a form coined at `m` and heard by all makes every formation tell `m` from `m'` again, so more distinctions after. S: `kept_rests` (l. 1294): records keep growing while the resolution rests. B: `TwoFormations.crossing_never_agrees` (l. 1454): the two exchange forms for ever. B: `TwoFormations.homonym` (l. 1518): agreement at one sense merges two senses. B: `Gloss.uptake_loses` (l. 1666): adding a record loses the resolution without replacing it.
places.how_read: Every declaration's statement and docstring read, l. 1-1675, with most proof bodies. Answers are from statements except rank (N with a D note on the account); nothing is U.

places.place: ShownOrder.lean: ChoiceOccasions.Shown, Accords, accorded_iff_noCycle, above_in_every_iff_reach, both_ways_of_unreached, weakly_forces_no_comparison, Untried.same_search_after
places.states: S: General, for every carrier `α` and every family of occasions `O`. Some strict order accords with the choices exactly where the shown relation has no cycle (`accorded_iff_noCycle`, l. 139). With no cycle, the positive comparisons every strict according order shares are exactly the shown reach (`above_in_every_iff_reach`, l. 148). Beyond the reach, orders rank two unreached alternatives both ways (`both_ways_of_unreached`, l. 262), and weak accord forces no comparison (`weakly_forces_no_comparison`, l. 275). B: `Untried`: one search, run with either of two strict according orders, chooses alike on the menu met and apart on the menu met after (`same_search_met`, l. 414; `same_search_after`, l. 421).
places.moves: S: `ChoiceOccasions` (l. 83): at each occasion an open set (`menu o : α → Prop`) and a choice (`pick o`). It is not a `Process`. The laws concern every strict relation according with the choices (`Accords`, l. 98), not what a choice keeps. B: `Untried.search` (l. 371) is one choice procedure run with two orders.
places.reading: S: `Shown` (l. 94) is what the choices register: `x` above `y` where at some occasion `x` is chosen while `y ≠ x` is open. `reach_within` (l. 123): every transitive according relation contains the shown reach. `above_in_every_iff_reach` (l. 148): what every strict order consistent with what is registered shares is exactly the shown reach. `above_in_some_of_unreached` (l. 251) and `both_ways_of_unreached` (l. 262): nothing beyond it is decided. B: `Untried.same_search_after` (l. 421): two orders that accord with what was registered choose apart on a later menu.
places.share: N: no shares in any statement read.
places.level: N: no level in any statement read.
places.giving: N: nothing gives to anything in any statement read.
places.cost: N: no cost in any statement read.
places.multiplying: N: no units or kinds that multiply.
places.no_return: N: no irreversibility in any statement read.
places.both_outcomes: N for going on against ending, or keeping against losing. The exactly-when statements are of another kind: `accorded_iff_noCycle` (l. 139) gives an exactly-when for the existence of a strict according order, and `noCycle_withPair_iff` (l. 237) gives one for a pair being added without a cycle.
places.comparison: S: `reach_within` (l. 123): every transitive relation according with the choices contains the shown reach, so the shown reach is covered by each. `above_in_class_of_every` (l. 158): every relation of a narrower class of strict according orders makes each comparison that every strict according order makes. B: `Untried.both_accord` (l. 398) with `same_search_met` (l. 414) and `same_search_after` (l. 421): two orders, one search.

places.states: Under the continuation condition `Unrestricted sig`, taken as a hypothesis, the module proves general laws: retaining what has significance is inclusion of what can form, adding is exceeding, and widening is retaining and adding, from every standpoint alike. It also proves general laws about rivals: a rival is exactly a point lacking significance; no statement reading only the dynamics entails the condition; and that excluding every rival gives the condition is exactly double-negation elimination. Built witnesses (Clearing, Transfer, Restoring.Inflow, Preemption) instantiate these.
places.moves: N: no `Process` with moves, no policy and no allowed set. Two level paths `l l' : Nat → C → Nat` are compared, and in the witnesses a part is present or withheld (`flow.WithheldLevels`), which is a premise, not a choice among steps.
places.reading: S: `ReadsOnlyDynamics` (l. 277) is a statement whose truth does not change with the significance. `ReadsOnlyDynamics.admits_rival` (l. 288): such a statement, holding with one significance, holds with a bounded rival. `ReadsOnlyDynamics.not_entails` (l. 297): given a standpoint and a formation, if such a statement entails `Unrestricted`, it holds of no dynamics. `Web.retains_agree` (l. 319): under `Unrestricted`, retaining from any two standpoints agrees. The significance `sig` is a free predicate, not an observation.
places.share: N: no count or fraction of one kind among several, and no rule set from one.
places.level: S: `Web.UnderminingOn.not_retains_unrestricted` (l. 356): if an event undermines at step t on condition c, every formation requiring c keeps requiring it at t+1 at no smaller `need`, and l admits each of them at t+1, then under `Unrestricted` the levels `W.level` do not retain along l. Levels are handed-in functions `l : Nat → C → Nat` with needs. No law of what comes back depending on what is left. D: the account (l. 47-56) names margin laws (`Flow.Balances.retains_iff_within_margin` and others) stated in Becoming.Retaining, not here.
places.giving: N in the general laws: levels are functions handed in. B: `Restoring.Inflow.retains_adds` (l. 465): the giver's part, under `Unrestricted`, retains and adds against the levels without it. `Clearing.clearer_loses_dweller` (l. 411): the clearer's part loses the dweller, a formation of the built model.
places.cost: N: no statement in which keeping or giving costs the one that does it. `Clearing.clearer_loses_dweller` (l. 411) states that the clearer is supported at every step and admitted without its part, so withholding the part costs it nothing.
places.no_return: B: `Preemption.not_undermining_yet_loses` (l. 483), concluded: in the built web, `false` is admitted at every step without the drawer's part and supported at no step after the first with it, while the drawer's event is active and not undermining. Under `Unrestricted` the part does not retain. `Clearing.clearer_loses_dweller` (l. 411): with the clearer's part the dweller is unsupported (used through `unsupported_with`). No general point of no return.
places.both_outcomes: S: `Web.retains_iff_includes` (l. 309) and `Web.keeps_iff_retains` (l. 333) are exactly-whens of retaining under `Unrestricted`. `unrestricted_iff_not_rival` (l. 260): where significance is decided, the condition holds iff no rival. These are not dichotomies of going on and ending. B: `Clearing.time_bounded_permits` (l. 438): in one model the clearer's part retains under `boundedInTime 1` and does not retain under `Unrestricted`.
places.comparison: S: `Web.Retains`/`Web.Adds` compare two level paths. `Retains.within` (l. 350): under `Unrestricted`, what retains from a standpoint retains under every bounded region. `retains_agree` (l. 319) carries retaining between standpoints. `widens_iff_retains_adds` (l. 325), `keeps_iff_retains` (l. 333) and `mixed_iff_adds` (l. 342) carry the orders of what can form to the orders of significance. B: `Transfer.unordered` (l. 449): each path adds what the other lacks.
places.rank: N.
places.closed_region: N: no invariant or region closed under steps. `rival_of_outside` (l. 189) and `bounded_rival` (l. 196) concern a region of standpoints, steps and formations within which a significance holds, not closure under steps.
places.forms_change: S: `Web.widens_iff_retains_adds` (l. 325): under `Unrestricted`, the levels l widen l' (more can form) iff they retain and add what has significance. B: `Restoring.Inflow.retains_adds` (l. 465): the giver's part adds a continuation with significance.

places.states: General laws of every world: in a finite world with decided activity, arising recurs iff ceasing recurs (l. 255), and asked without decidedness that law is equivalent to excluded middle (l. 1018); with a covering family balanced and dissipated from T and embodied arising, that the world rests cannot be refuted (l. 276); an amount not rising from T stops falling, unrefuted (l. 154). Built worlds (shuttle, selfDrawing, mutualism, drawdown, grazing, seedbank, leaking, throughput, flicker, accretion, attrition, undecided) show that each premise is contingent (l. 1025), that infinite worlds separate arising from ceasing (l. 1043), that living crosses arising (l. 1064), and that each premise of rest is needed (l. 1092).
places.moves: N: a World has a fixed flow and web; there is no choice among steps.
places.reading: N: no observation or class read alike. `World.Living` (l. 200), every active relatum not undermining, is a predicate on the world; `living_crosses` (l. 1064, built) shows that arising and ceasing do not decide it.
places.level: S: `Web.embodiedArising_stops_unrefuted` (l. 172): for a family ds balanced and dissipated from T, it cannot be that after every step a later embodied arising in ds stays unrefuted; the proof runs through the family's stock not rising. `falls_stop_unrefuted` (l. 154) and `World.rests_unrefuted_covering` (l. 276) give rest under covering, balance, dissipation and embodied arising. B: `drawdown_world` (l. 430): the parent's taking leaves the pool below its need. `seedbank_world` (l. 849): soil at level 1 below the seed's need of 2. No law here of what comes back depending on what is left.
places.giving: S, in part: the stock in `rests_unrefuted_covering` (l. 276) is the standing of the world's own relata, and only relata present in the flow give or take. `World.Acting` (l. 209), that only active relata give, is a premise that `contingent` (l. 1025) shows some worlds lack. B: in `grazing_world` (l. 777) the pool, a never-active relatum, is drawn by the grazer, and `grazing_browser_ends` (l. 792) concludes that the browser depending on it is not active after the step.
places.cost: B: `SelfDrawing.undermines` (l. 345) and `selfDrawing_world` (l. 366): the holder draws on its own standing as it hands it on, leaving its own dependence unmet, so not every event is living. In `Leaking` (l. 886, `leaking_world` l. 904) the holder takes its own unit and gives nothing, and balance fails.
places.multiplying: B: `drawdown` (l. 398), a parent drawing a pool down as it gives to two descendants; `accretion` (l. 537), where formation f arises across step f. No general law of the number of units by the step.
places.no_return: S: `World.not_recurring_of_rests_unrefuted` (l. 263) and `rests_unrefuted_covering` (l. 276): rest is concluded only as not refutable, and then neither arising nor ceasing recurs. B: `grazing_browser_ends` (l. 792), concluded: the browser is not active at step 1 because its dependence persists at the same need with the pool drawn below it, a loss at the loss of what it draws on. `restless_world` (l. 494): no reserve carries activity beyond support at every step. `seedbank_world` (l. 849): undermining with no ending.
places.both_outcomes: S: `World.arising_iff_ceasing` (l. 255), general: in a finite world with decided activity, arising recurs exactly when ceasing recurs. `arising_iff_ceasing_covering` (l. 247) is the covering form; `law_iff_em` (l. 1018) shows the law without decidedness is excluded middle. B: `living_crosses` (l. 1064), `separate` (l. 1043) and `rests_needs` (l. 1092) give dichotomies across built worlds, not both outcomes of one model.
places.comparison: S, weak: `ceasingRecurs_ofRoles` (l. 235): ceasing recurs in the two-kind world `ofRoles L W` iff some formation of W ceases at arbitrarily late steps. `World.law_iff_positions` (l. 1114) and `law_iff_grammar_positions` (l. 1124) relate the law to the grammar's positions. No simulation and no order carried by the step.
places.rank: S: `falls_stop_unrefuted` (l. 154): for q : Nat → Nat not rising from T, it is not the case that after every step from T a later fall stays unrefuted. `unrefuted_falls_exceed` (l. 128): if falls stayed unrefuted, q would exceed every bound. `amount_still_unrefuted` (l. 161): that q stays constant from some step cannot be refuted. This is a falling natural number, with no explicit time bound and no decision procedure.
places.closed_region: B: `leaking_world` (l. 904): the family [true, false] is `ClosedAt` every step and taken from at every step. `rests_unrefuted_covering` (l. 276) takes as a premise a list covering the active relata from T. No general invariant or kernel law here.
places.forms_change: B: `shuttle_world` (l. 310): a finite world where two sides hand one standing back and forth, arising and ceasing recur, and every event is living, so the going on continues while what stands alternates. `throughput_world` (l. 514) burns fresh fuel each step; `accretion` (l. 537) adds formations.

places.states: General laws on the counts of censuses of what stands and what depends under each selection of premises. Under balance, dissipation and enclosure from T, the total standing at T bounds change (l. 302), and a change bound is a law exactly when balance and dissipation are selected (l. 494, 681). The premises add nothing to counting dependences (l. 805, 817, 926). Built queues and rings witness that every tally is met.

places.states: General laws of a stock observable σ : S → Nat drawn on and replenished by the actions of every Process: balance at each step is balance along every course, a course of the stock process is executable exactly when it is covered (with a closed form by prefixes), a course repeated without end needs its replenishment to cover its draw, and an unending run is carried exactly when each draw is within the stock then standing. A level that falls by each draw, where anything positive draws, ends at nothing within as many steps as it holds; the only built case is accumulating (a stock that only replenishes).
places.moves: S: `covered_of_trace` (l. 191): for every Process P whose stock is Balanced and DrawsHeld, every course (Trace) from s is Covered from σ s. `product_feasible_iff` (l. 199): a course of the stock process run jointly with any process R is Feasible exactly when the stock covers it and R admits it. `trace_falls` (l. 537): under FallsBy, every course keeps σ t + total draw ≤ σ s. These are laws about every course among the process's steps; no policy or chosen subset is singled out.

places.states: In general, for every web, flow and world, transmission (`Flow.TransmitsWithin`) is inheritance together with the need within δ (`Flow.transmitsWithin_iff`, l. 462), and dropping one dependence of a giver keeps the seven other premises and finiteness while it breaks transmission, so transmission is independent wherever it binds (`World.drop_but`, l. 836), no condition kept by such a drop derives it (`World.vacuous_of_drop_invariant`, l. 854), and in a finite, balanced, dissipative, embodied world where activity needs support, the reading of drawing together with the link that drawing is depending gives it (`World.transmitting_of_drawn`, l. 899). It also characterises in general where a dependence forms anew at a descent (`Web.four_cases`, `Web.formsAnew_iff_drawn_unheld`, `Flow.formed_from_drawing`), with built cases that show each premise is needed (`droppedHatch`, `novel`, `bearingHatch`, `TwoGivers`, `Split`, `Drawdown.carried`).
places.moves: N: no process with a choice among steps (no `Process S A`, policy or allowed set) appears. The `Flow` has fixed `present`, `give` and `take`, and every law is about its descents (`DescendsAt`), not about a choice.
places.reading: S: `World.vacuous_of_drop_invariant` (l. 854) says: for any condition R on worlds that is kept by dropping one dependence, if R implies `Transmitting` then in a world meeting R transmission does not bind. What R does not register (the dropped dependence) cannot decide transmission. `Flow.DependsOnDrawn.drop` (l. 678) and `DependsOnFed.drop` (l. 683) state that the 'readings of the exchange' do not see a dropped dependence, and `World.drawn_not_enough` (l. 994) concludes that the drawing reading with finiteness and the seven other premises does not give transmission. Note that here a 'reading' is a condition on worlds (dependence only on what givers drew on), not an observation or a class of things read alike. N for an observation in that sense.
places.share: N: no count or fraction of one kind among several, and no rule set again from one.
places.level: S: `World.stock_le_start` (l. 863) says that in a balanced, dissipative world listed without repetition by `all`, the total standing `stock all t` never exceeds `stock all 0`. `World.Finite.level_le` (l. 874) says that in a finite, balanced, dissipative world every level is at most the total standing at the first step. `Flow.inherited_within_at` (l. 567) and `inherited_within` (l. 589) say that with balance at the condition over a stretch, inheritance and the need within δ at the descent, and the giver supported, the descendant's need plus everything taken from the condition since step S is at most its level at S plus everything given since, plus δ. `Flow.descendant_supported_at` (l. 625) bounds a supported descendant's need plus what was taken by the level plus what was given. So a level is drawn down, and a later need is bounded by what is left. N for a return that depends on what is left.
places.giving: S: `Flow.descends_of_comes` (l. 501) says that with balance at x, if x comes to stand across a step then some g present in the step gives to it (`DescendsAt`), so standing is given by a relatum of the model. `Flow.inherited_from_giver` (l. 511) and `no_new_dependence` (l. 531) say each dependence a relatum holds as it comes to stand was held by some giver, and where nothing taking part depends on c, nothing coming to stand does. That the giver can itself be lost is N: no statement about a giver ceasing to stand.
places.cost: N: nothing states that giving draws on the giver's own level or standing. In `TwoGivers.web` (l. 1109) the givers stand at one throughout while each gives the child one unit.
places.multiplying: B: a child coming to stand by descent from a parent in `finiteHatch_descends` (l. 923), `novel` (`World.link_without_drawn`, l. 969) and `TwoGivers.descends_first`/`descends_second` (l. 1175, 1178), the child given its standing by two givers. N for a law of the step by which the number of units changes.
places.no_return: N: no irreversibility and no point of no return. `World.drop` is a neighbouring world, not a later state. `Flow.no_new_dependence` (l. 531) is about one step: under balance and inheritance, where nothing taking part depends on c, nothing coming to stand depends on c after it.
places.both_outcomes: S: for keeping versus forming a dependence, not for going on versus ending. `Web.four_cases` (l. 294) says that where the giver's holding and drawing are decided, a descendant depending on c meets exactly one of four cases: held and drew, or held without drawing (inherited), or drew without holding, or neither (formed anew). `Web.inheritsAt_iff_not_formsAnew` (l. 250) says inheritance holds exactly when nothing forms anew, given stability. `World.transmitting_iff_inherits` (l. 892) says that in a finite, balanced, dissipative, embodied world where activity needs support, transmission holds exactly when inheritance does for every condition. `split_iff_em` (l. 413) says that forming and holding make inheritance at every descent exactly when excluded middle holds. places.place: TreeSearch.lean: scan, advance, scan_sound, exhausted_dead, scan_settles, inhabited_discovered, run_reads_scan, orbit_fixed, coherent_fork, fork_burden
places.states: This is one built model of a finite tree search (`Tree`, `scan`, `discover`, and the step law `advance` on `Search` configurations), with laws stated for every tree and frontier within it: what is found is real from a coherent frontier (`scan_sound`, l. 165), exhausted means no inhabited entry was on the frontier (`exhausted_dead`, l. 194), fuel of at least the frontier's node count settles the search (`scan_settles`, l. 219), and an inhabited tree is found with fuel of its node count (`inhabited_discovered`, l. 236). Along every run of `Law.process advance`, step n reads as the scan with fuel n (`run_reads_scan`, l. 357), so each scan law is restated as a law of the runs.
places.moves: S: `run_reads_scan` (l. 357) and `run_reads_discover` (l. 363) say that for every run r of `Law.process advance` starting at ⟨f, none, 0⟩ (or `start root`), `read (r.state n) = scan n f` (or `discover n root`). The run laws `inspected_le_step` (l. 392), `found_located` (l. 397), `exhausted_dead_run` (l. 408), `steps_settle` (l. 413) and `inhabited_found` (l. 419) hold for every run. The process is that of one determined law (`advance`), so the statements cover every run but no real choice among steps. N for a law about what one choice keeps against another.
places.reading: S: `exhausted_dead` (l. 194) says that if the scan's verdict is `exhausted` then `live frontier = false`, so the verdict decides only absence within the frontier. `scan_sound` (l. 165) says that from a frontier coherent with root, a ticket found satisfies `locate root ticket.1 = some ticket.2`. `found_without_complete_map` (l. 265) says that for every key and every `unread` subtree, `discover 2 (.fork (.endpoint key) unread) = ⟨.found ([false], key), 2⟩`: the verdict does not depend on the unread subtree. `read` (l. 307) is the verdict a configuration shows.
places.share: N: no count or fraction of one kind among several, and no rule set again from one.
places.level: S: within one model, the fuel of `scan` (def l. 106) falls by one per inspection, and the verdict is `pending` when it reaches 0 with a nonempty frontier. `scan_settles` (l. 219) says that if `burden frontier ≤ fuel` the verdict is not `pending`. `scan_fuel` (l. 139) says inspected ≤ fuel. N for a level where what comes back depends on what is left.
places.giving: N: nothing gives to a level or keeps a condition met.
places.cost: S (weak): each inspection uses one unit of the search's fuel (def `scan`, l. 106), and `scan_fuel` (l. 139) says `(scan fuel frontier).inspected ≤ fuel`. `inspected_le_step` (l. 392) says that on every run `(r.state n).inspected ≤ n`. N for a cost to the one that keeps or gives.
places.multiplying: S: in the scan and in `advance` (l. 291), a fork entry is replaced by its two children on the frontier. `fork_burden` (l. 206) says the burden of the frontier with the fork equals the burden after opening it plus 1. This is a step law on the number of entries in one built model.
places.no_return: S, concluded: `advance_found` (l. 313) says a configuration with a ticket found is left unchanged, `advance_empty` (l. 317) says one with nothing left and none found is left unchanged, and `orbit_fixed` (l. 320) says a configuration fixed by `advance` is its whole orbit. These are absorbing states at the end of the search, not at the loss of something that gives.
places.both_outcomes: S, in this model: the `Verdict` (l. 92) is found, exhausted or pending. Together, `inhabited_discovered` (l. 236), which says that if `nodes root ≤ fuel` and root is inhabited a real ticket is found, `exhausted_dead` (l. 194) and `scan_settles` (l. 219) give both outcomes for every tree once fuel reaches its node count, though no single 'exactly when' is stated. `interrupted_pending` (l. 269, built) shows pending with too little fuel and found with more. N for going on versus ending of a going-on in the map's sense.
places.comparison: S: `orbit_reads_scan_from` (l. 326) and `orbit_reads_scan` (l. 351) carry the recursive scan to the orbit of the step law: `read (Law.orbit advance ⟨f, none, 0⟩ n) = scan n f`. `run_reads_scan` (l. 357) carries that to every run of `Law.process advance`. `child_locate` (l. 130) and `coherent_fork` (l. 152) carry coherence between a frontier and the tree.
places.rank: S: `scan_settles` (l. 219) says the search ends, not pending, within fuel equal to the frontier's burden (node count), with burden falling by one at each fork opened (`fork_burden`, l. 206). `steps_settle` (l. 413) says that on every run, if `burden f ≤ n` the verdict at step n is not pending. `inhabited_found` (l. 419) says an inhabited tree is found within `nodes root` steps. `located_depth_le` (l. 246) says a located address has length + 1 ≤ nodes root.
places.closed_region: S: `coherent_fork` (l. 152) and `coherent_tail` (l. 148) say coherence of the frontier with the tree is kept by opening a fork and by passing an entry (an invariant). `orbit_fixed` (l. 320) with `advance_found` and `advance_empty` gives fixed points of the step law.
places.forms_change: B (weak): in `pending_then_found` (l. 374) and `interrupted_pending` (l. 269), the search is pending at step 1 and found at step 3, so an interrupted search is not an absence and more steps find more. In this model the frontier's entries change at every step while the search goes on (def `advance`, l. 291). N for a relay, an alternation or kinds coming and going.

places.place: TurningInTime.lean: turns_in_time_iff, turns_in_time_iff_kept_below, unending_iff_above, unending_iff_first_marked, ends_with_net_regime, ends_with_net_rising, recoverable_iff_above, noReturnAt_iff_first_below, turns_in_time_iff_before, locked_turns_in_time_on_window_iff, locked_ends_with_net_regime, locked_closed, Three
places.states: The module defines a pair of a way and a level stepped by `pair after left`, cut by a need (`net`, a `Law.stepWhile`). It proves general laws for every way type, step and level step that meet their premises: when the way's class is constant (`toEnd_iff`, `constant_iff`); that the line ends within a bound where the net ends (`ends_with_net`, `ends_with_net_regime`, `ends_with_net_rising`); exactly when the line never ends, namely when the way turns at the first marked level to a kept kind while the level is still at or above H₂ + y₂ (`unending_iff_first_marked`, `unending_iff_above`, `turns_in_time_iff`, `turns_in_time_iff_kept_below`); the lock's courses read as courses of the pair (`locked_closed`, `locked_ends_with_net_regime`, `locked_turns_in_time_on_window_iff`); and a point of no return, a level and a step, joined (`recoverable_iff_above`, `noReturnAt_iff_first_below`, `turns_in_time_iff_before`). Built cases on one numeric model are in namespace `Three` (giving min z (12 - z), uses 5 and 3, need 1, start 9).
places.moves: S: `pair_adaptive` (l. 352) states that the pair's step is `Mechanism.adaptive`'s `moveRel` at the single move `()`, and `constant_adaptive` (l. 415) states that at need 0 the way's class is constant under the net exactly when it is constant under that `moveRel` for every `u : Unit`. N: no other process has a choice among steps. Every law is of one deterministic step (`Law.step` or `Law.stepWhile` of `pair after left`), with `after`, `alone`, `marked` and the reading schedule `reads` handed in. The laws hold for every such function that meets their premises; no run makes a choice.
places.reading: S: `AloneOutside marked alone after` (def l. 368) says that at every unmarked level the way after a step is `alone` of the way; the marked levels are the ones that make a difference. `toEnd_iff` (l. 380) states that the way's class is constant up to the net's end exactly when no two levels that meet the need give one way two different ways. `turns_in_time_iff` (l. 1129) states that whether the line never ends is decided at the first marked level of the course as it was. On the lock, `windowAfter` (l. 1330) reads the rule off the level through `windowRead` at levels in [N, K), and off the share by `hA` elsewhere (`window_alone_outside`, l. 1604). `locked_turns_in_time_on_window_iff` (l. 1692) states that, under its premises, a `Locked` way below H₁ + y₁ never ends exactly when its first step at a level the window reads leaves the level at or above H₂ + y₂. `window_corrected` (l. 1648) states that where every step reads and `hL` gives a `kept` rule in [N, K), the rule after such a step is `kept`. B: `Three.unlocked_goes_on` (l. 2965) is a course that never ends while no step is at a level the window reads.
places.share: S: the lock's share is an abstract `A` with a preorder `P`, and the rule `R` is read off it by `hA` (`windowAlone`, l. 1338). Under `Raises`, `ReadsShare` and favouring kept upward, `locked_alone` (l. 1360) states that a `Locked` share and rule stay `Locked` along `windowAlone`. `locked_alone_not_below` (l. 1415) states that the share and rule never fall below the start's. `count_rises` (l. 1532) covers the case where the share is a natural-number count that every favouring rule raises strictly and the use is that count times u > 0: then the use rises under each step. `windowAfterShare` (l. 1788) and `locked_turns_in_time_share_iff` (l. 1876) cover a window that sets the share as well as the rule. N: no share is a fraction of one kind among several kinds of units.
places.level: S: the level steps by `RegimeMargin.step giving (use w) x`. `regime_step_eq` (l. 557) states that this is x + giving (x - d) - d when giving 0 = 0, so what comes back depends on what is left after the use. `held_above` (l. 889) states that a positive level c which a step under a use U ≥ H does not lower is at or above H + y, given nothing from nothing and giving short of H below y. `ends_with_net_regime` (l. 611) states that from a level below H + y, with uses of at least H along `alone`'s orbit and a positive need no marked level meets, the line ends within x steps. `rising_takes_all` (l. 675) states that, against a cap hi and a use rising strictly for hi steps, the level is 0 at step hi + 1.
places.giving: N: in every law `giving : Nat → Nat` is a function handed in, under the premises `RegimeMargin.FromNothing`, `Short`, `Meets` and `Keeps`. It is not a going-on of the model that can be lost. D: the account (l. 276-279) says the way enters the level's step only through `use`, with one `giving` for every way.
places.cost: N: no statement charges a turn, or the keeping of the kept kind, to the way that does it. The kept kind's use H₂ is a premise (`uses`), and the turn is given (`turns`). The level is drawn by the way's own use (`RegimeMargin.step giving (use w)`, in `ends_with_net_regime` l. 611 and `turns_in_time_iff` l. 1129). That is the line's own level running down under its use, not a cost of keeping or giving.
places.multiplying: N: no units leave units and no kinds form kinds. `count_rises` (l. 1532) raises a natural-number share by one under a favouring rule, which is a number, not units.
places.no_return: S, concluded: section 7 does this for any level course X that never rises and starts at most hi, with the feasible courses being X turned to a standing use H (`turned`, `Turned`, l. 1999-2005) and with the need met at every step as what is asked (`MeetsNeed`). Under FromNothing, Short, Meets and Keeps and a positive need at most H + y: `recoverable_iff_above` (l. 2146) states that X is recoverable at N exactly when H + y ≤ X N; `noReturnAt_iff_first_below` (l. 2159) states that its point of no return is the first step whose level is below H + y; `noReturnAt_of_below` (l. 2207) and `noReturn_exists` (l. 2311) state that one exists, within x steps on the course as it was.
